docs.title: CheckOwners
docs.text:
Local-first documentation for inferring CODEOWNERS from git history. The repository is smusali/checkowners.

Zero telemetry, ever, by default. CheckOwners does not phone home. Network use is opt-in GitHub API access.

docs.title: Five-minute audit
docs.text:
Install the core package and audit the repository you are in. Git 2.23.0 or newer is required, and the clone needs full history.

pip install checkowners
checkowners audit

uvx checkowners audit runs the same command without a permanent install. With no subcommand, checkowners runs audit. checkowners --help still prints help.

Exit status is the same for every command. The codes are in Exit codes.

docs.title: CI setup
docs.text:
The composite Action needs a full clone. A shallow checkout fails before analysis starts.

permissions:
  contents: read
steps:
  - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    with:
      fetch-depth: 0
  - uses: smusali/checkowners@v0
    with:
      comment_on_pr: false

Inputs, outputs, and the comment and SARIF options are in Action. Workflow examples stay in GitHub Actions.

docs.title: Generate CODEOWNERS
docs.text:
checkowners generate

The command writes inferred owners into the generated block and leaves a manual block unchanged. Dialects, round-trip checks, and the file layout are in Generated CODEOWNERS.

docs.text:

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• A documentation site, published from this repository, with search, a version per release, and the adoption guide for an existing large repository.
  • .checkowners-baseline.json is excluded from analysis by default, so refreshing the accepted-findings file does not create a single-expert finding about the file itself.
  • The contributor guide names the maintainer seat, the contributor ladder, the open-core boundary, the zero-telemetry guarantee, the AI-assisted review process, semantic versioning, and the release pipeline. Architectural decisions are in docs/decisions.md. CITATION.cff records citation metadata.
  • RepositoryAnalyzer is the library entry point. analyze() returns scored ownership with the commit, blame, and review observations stored on each path. The same observations are written into the state file and can be scored again with score_owners without another git or API pass. A state file written before this field still loads.
  • generate and validate take --dialect github|gitlab|bitbucket|gerrit. GitHub output is unchanged. GitLab writes one [Section][1] per top-level directory, and ^[Section] only when every owner on that directory is below the confidence threshold. Bitbucket and Gerrit exit 2. RepositoryAnalyzer.reconcile() reports declared-local, declared-global, and observed owners at file, directory, package, service, and repository scope.
  • checkowners calibrate back-tests ownership scores against later authors. calibrate --fit writes per-repository weights and a provenance block when history spans at least 180 days and at least 30 labeled paths. The result is held-out performance. A public validation corpus and harness record the same metrics, baselines, and a calibration curve.
  • checkowners report --html writes one offline HTML file with an overview, treemap, ownership map, historical timeline, team alignment, and drill-down. Anonymize and aggregate-only modes remove identities. A report names its head SHA, generation time, and analysis completeness, and shows evidence quality beside each score.
  • A public false-positive ledger records the prediction, the judgment, the reason, the fix, and the original evidence. Fixed entries name a regression test. New reports use the false-positive issue form.
  • A dataset generator writes per-repository HTML and JSON, a 50-audit list, counts, and checksums. README self-audit badges report ownership coverage, critical knowledge-risk paths, and CODEOWNERS drift.
  • cache info reports the current repository id, its state file path, and whether that file exists. A repository with no state file exits 1. A directory that is not a git repository exits 2.
  • A benchmark harness records cold, warm, and incremental analyze runs. Pull-request CI runs the synthetic tier. Public repositories stay on a manual workflow until their commit is pinned.
  • Blame coverage is cached by blob SHA, path, blame flags, ignore-revs, mass-refactor revisions, and .mailmap. cache info counts those files. cache clear removes them. --verbose prints hit and miss counts. --no-cache skips the cache.
  • Blame stays one git blame process per path. owners, explain, and change blame only the path they were asked about.
  • Ownership scoring is ownership-v2. Change survival is current blame lines divided by that person's lines at their last commit. Default weights are recency 0.30, frequency 0.20, blame 0.20, review 0.15, and change survival 0.15. A survival below 0.2 with a later commit from someone else is superseded. At or above 0.2, later commits no longer mark the owner superseded. A pin of ownership-v1 is rejected. The ci benchmark tier records the cold and warm cost.
  • History follows renames and same-commit copies by default (analysis.follow_renames, analysis.rename_similarity). explain shows the prior names, logical file id, and rename confidence. analysis.follow_renames: false keeps each literal path separate.
  • checkowners audit is the command run when no subcommand is given. checkowners --help still prints help. checkowners doctor and checkowners doctor --env report configuration and environment rows. A missing token or a failed API row is unverifiable.
  • Drift compares a team rule with the expanded member set. Statuses are aligned, partial-drift, unverifiable, invisible, empty, and nested. Each team record carries the snapshot timestamp. An offline run does not read the cache into aligned.
  • The local syntax validator is diffed against GitHub's CODEOWNERS errors endpoint. corpus/conformance.json publishes the pass rate. A private non-default branch that returns no errors is excluded. A weekly workflow opens or updates an issue when the rate drops and does not commit.
  • Drift severity is a score of overlap, confidence delta, path criticality, decay, and a single qualified owner. The default cutoffs are 0.15, 0.35, 0.55, and 0.75. Below the first cutoff the tier is info, which SARIF reports as note.
  • checkowners graph exports DOT (the documented default), GraphML, GEXF, and JSON. Text and JSON include articulation points, unweighted betweenness, orphan files, and a --from/--to transfer path. DOT, GraphML, and GEXF stay valid exports; a transfer path for those formats is printed on stderr. An unknown --export value exits 2 and lists the supported formats.
  • checkowners onboard lists experimental inferred suggestions. Steps follow resolved Python imports when those edges exist, name a cycle and fall back to path order when they do not, and list the signals that were not available. Mentor candidates exclude former, inactive, and bot contributors.
  • checkowners topology reports weighted Louvain clusters (topology-v2) with seed 0, --resolution, modularity, and cross-seed stability. Output is experimental. Declared teams are compared with Jaccard, precision, recall, and coverage. Co-change and temporal collaboration are reported as unavailable.
  • Identity resolution prefers a configured identities entry, then noreply parsing, this repository's handle cache, author.login on a local commit, and user search last. Search does not merge two owners. Misses expire after identity.negative_cache_ttl_days. identity merge, identity unmerge, and identity audit record or report identity changes without a second cache. contributors.roster sets contributor_status, including former, and risk reports former_knowledge_share. simulate --remove-status removes cached owners with that status. Bot detection adds configured addresses, account type, and a frequency cap for repeated mechanical subjects.
  • The nightly Fuzz workflow publishes mutation scores for patterns.py, drift.py, generate.py, the analyze.py scoring path, and the GitHub identity helpers. patterns.py fails when its score is below 90.
  • drift, risk, and validate accept --format text|json|sarif|junit. --json remains the shortcut for JSON. SARIF 2.1.0 uses seven stable rule ids, and the fingerprint is the baseline identity so a later severity change does not mint a new alert. The Action always writes checkowners.sarif and checkowners.junit.xml into the report artifact. upload_sarif uploads that file for a same-repo token that can write security-events. Fork and Dependabot pull requests keep the artifact and skip the upload. A workflow_run workflow uploads the artifact for those forks once that workflow file is on the default branch.
  • In GitHub Actions the same findings become workflow annotations, capped at 50, and a completed check run named checkOwners. A missing token or a 401, 403, or 404 leaves the job result unchanged. checks: write is the scope for the check run. .github/workflows/checkowners.yml is a reusable workflow for the composite action.
  • checkowners diff SPEC and checkowners suggest --diff SPEC report ownership impact and reviewer routing for the changed paths. suggest --pr N reads the pull request file list and does not request reviewers. --diff-only SPEC limits read-only analysis commands to those paths and does not replace the repository cache. Recommendations carry per-signal evidence. A high review-load band demotes someone only when the load signal is completed reviews or caller-supplied counts.
  • generate keeps a # checkowners:manual block byte for byte and rewrites only the generated block, output.block_order chooses which block wins overlapping paths, drift --fix-plan prints suggested edits without writing, and a manual rule that differs from observed expertise is reported for review rather than as changed.
  • Incremental analysis replays a usable baseline by default, --no-incremental forces a full lookback, and a rejected baseline is scored again from scratch with the reason printed.
  • CI tests Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows, limits each pull-request test job to 25 minutes, and covers Git 2.23.0 and Git 2.39.3 on Ubuntu for pushes, the nightly run, and manual runs.
  • checkowners suggest recommends one reviewer from expertise and current load, with balance as an alias and GitHub review load when a token sample exists.
  • policy chooses which finding classes block, warning by default for drift, a single expert, unowned paths, and incomplete analysis, and failing for invalid owners.
  • checkowners sync opens or updates one reconciliation pull request by default, while --commit commits on the current branch and --dry-run prints the diff only.
  • Co-authored-by trailers credit co-authors when git.count_co_authors is true, and analyze reports the detected merge_strategy plus co_author_count.
  • Recency uses each path's median commit gap as its half-life, and each owner reports expertise, maintenance recency, and a continuity-risk status.
  • checkowners simulate --remove reports paths that lose coverage and the repository truck factor before and after, using the cached map only.
  • qualified-owners reports a criticality-weighted distribution of top_owner_share, and an empty criticality map sets criticality_incomplete.
  • Per-path risk reports concentration from every ownership_score above the confidence threshold, while top_n_owners still caps only the displayed owner list.
  • The composite Action caches pip and ~/.checkowners, reusing a restored state file only when its commit is HEAD and the config hash and model versions match.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• model.topology is topology-v2. A config pin of topology-v1 is refused. Cached state and graph files from topology-v1 are ignored.
  • The ownership review factor reads closed pulls inside analysis.review_lookback_days through batched GraphQL queries, and a window cut short by the request budget records a gap and lowers analysis_completeness.
  • checkowners trends reports historical_activity_confidence (historical-v1) instead of avg_top_confidence, and --compare-ownership requires --acknowledge-different-metrics.
  • The Action fail_on_drift input defaults to empty so a run follows policy.drift.fail, and checkowners drift exits 3 only for a novel finding that policy marks as blocking.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text: • ROADMAP.md, docs/ACTION_ITEMS.md, and docs/PROJECT_STATE_AND_ROADMAP.md are removed, and release planning now lives in the issue tracker.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Path globs and paths.exclude treat \ and / as the same separator and stay case-sensitive on every operating system.
  • Git path output is read as UTF-8 with quoting disabled, CHECKOWNERS_STATE_DIR expands a leading tilde, and Git older than 2.23.0 exits 4 with the version to install.
  • requirements-dev.lock pins colorama 0.4.6 on Windows so hashed installs satisfy pytest there.
  • Concurrent handle-cache writes take an in-process lock, and a Windows file lock when another process may write the same cache.
  • requirements.lock and requirements-dev.lock pin PyJWT 2.15.1 and urllib3 2.8.0 so pip-audit no longer fails on the advisories in the previous pins.
  • All three lock files pin certifi 2026.10.19, which drops the emSign ECC Root CA - G3 root after its intermediates were compromised (PYSEC-2026-4320, GHSA-6q48-6c7w-9gw2).
Correctness and trust: scored ownership, schema 1, privacy controls, and supply-chain checks. Inference stays local git.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• docs/METHODOLOGY.md states the formulas, truck-factor divergence, terminology, golden beliefs, and principles, docs/limitations.md states when the tool can be wrong, and CI fails if a shipped metric key is missing from the methodology page.
  • The README leads with a drift example, install, run, CI, the offline guarantee, Trusted Publishing, and Sigstore, and adds examples/demo.gif, examples/pr-comment.png, and examples/sample-CODEOWNERS.
  • .pre-commit-hooks.yaml exposes checkowners-validate and checkowners-drift, this repository runs both, and the hooks are documented in docs/USAGE.md.
  • CI runs CodeQL, dependency review, pip-audit, and zizmor, Dependabot updates Python dependencies, and each GitHub Release carries a CycloneDX SBOM and a signed provenance attestation.
  • Human reports, the job summary, and pull-request comments state that CheckOwners is a knowledge-risk tool, not a performance-measurement tool, and docs/PRIVACY.md records the data flow, cache, cache purge, and threat model.
  • A public CODEOWNERS compatibility corpus (corpus/compatibility.jsonl) and a license-checked parser corpus (corpus/realworld.jsonl) ship under corpus/README.md.
  • Privacy controls add output.anonymize, output.aggregate_only, privacy.redact_emails with --redact-emails, identity.mode (handle, email, or hashed), and contributors.exclude, and the Action input include_balance defaults to false.
  • On-disk state is schema 1 with tokenized emails, atomic locked writes, reuse only when HEAD and the scoring config still match, cache path|info|clear|purge, a 256 MiB cap, and --offline with no network calls.
  • Analysis completeness is a run-level score with analysis_gaps that scales evidence quality only, and --fail-on-incomplete or policy.incomplete_analysis.fail exits 3 when a runtime, worker, API, or rate-limit bound leaves the run incomplete.
  • --json uses schema 1 (docs/schemas/commands-v1.json) with schema_version, checkowners_version, models, repository, head_sha, generated_at, and analysis_completeness, plus identity, flat signals, per-path risk, nested drift recommendation, optional GitHub evidence stamps, and Action summaries at integer schema_version: 1.
  • Configuration requires version: 1 and pins ownership-v1, risk-v1, and topology-v1, refuses any other version or unimplemented keys such as criticality, and ignores caches whose models do not match.
  • checkowners baseline create writes accepted findings identified by rule, path, and owner set, and --baseline, drift.baseline_file, CHECKOWNERS_BASELINE, the Action baseline input, and reasoned suppressions keep CI failing only on new findings.
  • checkowners explain PATH decomposes one path's inferred ownership, checkowners owners PATH (who) prints a ranked list, and both accept --json with schema_version: "1" without reading or writing the cache.
  • Analyze excludes linguist-generated and linguist-vendored paths from .gitattributes when analysis.respect_gitattributes is true, reports excluded_gitattributes and excluded_static, and falls back to paths.exclude.
  • Blame honors .git-blame-ignore-revs, ignores whitespace, detects moves and copies, omits mass-refactor commits above git.mass_refactor_file_fraction (default 0.5), and requires Git 2.23 or newer.
  • .mailmap is applied first when identity.mailmap is true, and analyze reports whether a mapping file was found.
  • generate and sync fail when re-resolved CODEOWNERS owners differ from the intended set, unless output.verify_round_trip is false.
  • generate warns at 2 MB and refuses above output.max_bytes (default 2_500_000) without --force, and --json includes bytes_written and rules_written.
  • checkowners explain-path <path> shows the winning CODEOWNERS rule and the full match chain.
  • generate and sync refuse sanitized * rules that would assign a different owner set, unless --allow-broad-patterns or output.allow_broad_patterns is set, and --json records broad_patterns.
  • Golden ownership tests in tests/test_golden.py record what ownership-v1 concludes for pinned git histories under a fixed as-of.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Action output checkowners_drift is now drift_summary in github-action --json and GITHUB_OUTPUT, and command JSON and Action summaries both use schema 1.
  • Commands share exit codes 0 clean, 1 internal, 2 usage, 3 findings, and 4 integration failure, with --exit-zero clearing only code 3 and --fail-on-incomplete exiting 3 when completeness is below 1.
  • The composite Action runs checkowners github-action once for drift, qualified owners, decay, the job summary, and GITHUB_OUTPUT.
  • Recency, decay, and lookback age against --as-of, else SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, else the HEAD committer time, JSON emits head_sha and generated_at, and drift.hysteresis_runs holds severity flips.
  • Ownership scoring renormalizes over available signals into ownership_score on [0, 1] with a separate evidence_quality, stamps models.ownership: ownership-v1, and no longer caps offline scores at 0.85.
  • The default qualification.strategy is adaptive, so commit count is evidence with Bayesian shrinkage rather than an eligibility gate, while threshold keeps a commit-count gate and undamped frequency.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • requirements-dev.lock pins pyyaml-ft to python_version >= "3.13" so hashed CI installs skip libcst's 3.13-only YAML backend on 3.11 and 3.12.
Corrective release: identity, Action supply chain, metric naming, and the contributor on-ramp. No new inference behavior.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Issue forms (bug, false-positive, feature), a pull-request template, Discussions, ROADMAP.md, the action-item register, .github/FUNDING.yml, two example configs, and demo assets (terminal recording, PR comment, sample analyze / drift JSON). Listing PRs: awesome-actions, awesome-devops, static-analysis.
  • A dev extra bootstraps tests and linters via pip install -e ".[dev]".
  • Python 3.14 classifier and CI matrix entry. checkowners/py.typed ships in the wheel so the Typing :: Typed classifier is accurate.
  • requirements-dev.lock pins CI test and lint installs with hashes.
  • pytest --cov-fail-under=85 so CI fails below the documented coverage floor. Branch coverage is collected repo-wide and reported for patterns.py, analyze.py, drift.py, and generate.py.
  • Ruff enables S (bandit), PTH (pathlib), RUF, C4, PL, ARG, TID, and ERA.
  • Coverage badge on the README pointing at smusali/checkowners.
  • Composite Action input max_output_entries (default 50) caps each list in the GITHUB_OUTPUT summaries. Full drift.json, bus_factor.json, and decay.json payloads are uploaded as the checkowners-reports artifact, exposed via the artifact_name output.
  • The composite Action always writes the drift, bus-factor, and decay report to the job summary, including when the drift step fails.
  • Third-party GitHub Actions are pinned to full commit SHAs. Dependabot watches the github-actions ecosystem, and CI fails on any unpinned uses: reference.
  • The publish workflow rejects a GitHub Release whose tag has no dated changelog heading.
  • The composite Action installs the checkowners version that matches its own tag from a committed wheel and a hashed requirements.lock. New index_url and offline inputs support internal mirrors and air-gapped runners. install_spec is limited to a local extras allowlist.
  • CI and the publish job fail when the Action pin, package version, wheel, or lockfile disagree with each other (or with the release tag).

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Codecov uploads authenticate with CODECOV_TOKEN and fail the job if the report is rejected, so the README coverage badge can receive data.
  • README monthly-download badge uses pepy.tech instead of shields.io pypi/dm, which was rendering "rate limited by upstream service".
  • CI pip installs retry with a longer timeout on transient PyPI index failures.
  • The Action PR-comment lookup paginates past 100 comments, so the managed comment is updated instead of duplicated. Interpolated paths, notes, and reasons are escaped, long paths are truncated, and the report is capped with an overflow line pointing at the uploaded artifact.
  • Composite Action multiline GITHUB_OUTPUT writes use a random ghadelim_ delimiter instead of a static EOF, so a path, note, or reason equal to EOF can no longer truncate or inject outputs.
  • The composite Action no longer installs an unpinned latest package from PyPI. uses: smusali/checkowners@vX.Y.Z now installs checkowners==X.Y.Z.
  • install_spec dogfood installs use pip's isolated build env so hatchling is available. git blame no longer crashes on non-UTF-8 files, and *.whl is excluded from inference.
  • README documentation and license links are now absolute GitHub URLs so they resolve on the PyPI project page.
  • The composite Action exports GITHUB_TOKEN on every CLI step via a github_token input (default ${{ github.token }}). The 0.5.0 claim that installing the github extra made handle resolution work in CI was incomplete: the extra was installed, but the token was never passed, so only local noreply parsing worked. When github.api_enabled is true and no token is reachable, the CLI now prints a warning naming GITHUB_TOKEN instead of degrading silently. The same input is now passed to the PR comment step, so a PAT or App token takes precedence over github.token.
  • PR comments no longer fail the job on fork pull requests or read-only workflow permissions. Forks skip the comment with a notice; a 403 becomes a warning that names pull-requests: write and comment_on_pr: false. The comment body is a short sectioned report rather than a details-block dump.
  • Solo-maintainer repos no longer get a per-file knowledge-risk comment for bus_factor = 1. The Action only lists single-owner paths when more than one human has qualified ownership, and names the owner and suggested backups instead of saying "bus factor 1".
  • The composite Action sets CHECKOWNERS_STATE_DIR to ${{ runner.temp }}/checkowners-state on every CLI step, so CI state no longer lands in the runner home directory. Environment variables (CHECKOWNERS_CONFIG, CHECKOWNERS_DRIFT_MODE, CHECKOWNERS_STATE_DIR, GITHUB_TOKEN, plus runner-provided GITHUB_REPOSITORY and GITHUB_OUTPUT) are documented with their precedence over the config file.
  • Composite Action description is under 125 characters so GitHub Marketplace will accept the listing.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• The all extra composes checkowners[graph,github] instead of duplicating those dependency lists. Runtime dependencies are capped at the next untested major. Package version is read from checkowners/__init__.py only.
  • Test and lint CI install from requirements-dev.lock with hashes instead of resolving a hatch environment unpinned.
  • The truncated owner count is now named qualified_owner_count. Human output always states the top_n_owners cap. JSON emits both qualified_owner_count and the deprecated bus_factor alias for one minor cycle, plus qualified_owner_count_cap and deprecated_keys. checkowners qualified-owners is the canonical command; bus-factor remains as a deprecated alias pending redefinition. Persisted state is schema v4; Action summaries are schema_version 2. README, PyPI, and Action copy no longer advertise an unqualified bus factor.
  • Composite Action outputs checkowners_drift, bus_factor_summary, and decay_summary are now bounded summaries (schema_version: 1) with counts and a truncated flag, not the full CLI payloads. Bus-factor entries are omitted from GITHUB_OUTPUT. fromJson gates on drift_detected, severity, and critical_paths[0] are unchanged.
  • Project URLs, documentation clone and issue links, the Actions example, and the security advisory link now point at this repository.
  • Changelog version dates are the PyPI publication day; the 0.3.0 and 0.5.0 headings now match those uploads.
  • Composite Action mode default is now commit, matching DriftConfig and the configuration reference. Callers who omitted mode previously got both (including stale-rule detection) and must pass mode: both to keep that behavior.
  • Positioning copy no longer claims priority. The comparison table credits competitors, including where they exceed CheckOwners (owner-existence checks, formal truck factor, compile-time check mode). The runtime sentence now matches the 0.5.0 dogfood figure of under three minutes on a 24k-commit, 12k-file monorepo. The README and FAQ state the AI-assistance posture explicitly: inference is deterministic git analysis, and the codebase has been built with reviewed agent assistance. Unused CLAUDE.md agent instructions are removed.

Hardening release driven by testing every command against a real production monorepo (24k commits, 12k active files). Focus: correct CODEOWNERS semantics, analyze performance, per-repo state isolation, and identity resolution.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• CODEOWNERS pattern matching engine (checkowners/patterns.py) with GitHub's documented gitignore-style semantics: * stays within a path segment, ** crosses segments, leading or interior / anchors to the repo root, trailing / matches directory contents, dir/* matches direct children only, and the last matching rule wins.
  • generate consolidates per-file inference into directory-level rules when every inferred file under a directory shares one owner set (/src/ @alice instead of hundreds of per-file lines). New files under a consolidated directory now match a rule. Disable with output.consolidate: false.
  • generate and sync refuse to overwrite a hand-written CODEOWNERS (one without the machine-generated header) unless --force is passed.
  • --version flag; running bare checkowners now prints help instead of a usage error.
  • Progress bar (stderr, TTY-only) during the analyze blame pass.
  • Local GitHub-noreply email resolution: 12345+login@users.noreply.github.com and login@users.noreply.github.com map to @login with zero API calls and no token.
  • Persistent email-to-handle cache at <state-dir>/handles.json, including remembered misses, so the rate-limited user-search API is only queried once per new email.
  • Identity merging: when several commit emails resolve to one GitHub handle, their owner entries merge and per-path bus factor is recomputed over distinct people, so one person with two emails no longer reads as a bus factor of two. Decay warnings are remapped to the resolved handle.
  • Drift results carry notes explaining skipped comparisons (raw emails vs @handles, team-owned rules) instead of emitting false drift.
  • balance reports fallback_reason when the GitHub API path was abandoned, and labels the load column "Commits (proxy)" when counting authorship.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Drift detection is now pattern-aware. Inferred files are matched against CODEOWNERS rules with real matching semantics; previously the comparison was literal string equality, so directory rules like frontend/ never matched inferred file paths and real-world files produced near-100% false "missing"/"stale" reports. New categories: missing = file no rule covers, stale = rule matching no tracked file (via git ls-files), changed = per-rule owner divergence, aggregated and ranked by worst per-file delta. Owner comparison is case-insensitive.
  • State is keyed per repo (schema v3) at ~/.checkowners/state/<repo-hash>.json with the absolute repo path embedded and verified on load. Previously a single global state.json meant analyzing repo A then running decay in repo B silently reused repo A's data.
  • Analyze is parallel and skips unowned files. git blame now runs on a thread pool sized to the CPU count and only on paths where at least one author reaches min_commits (4-5x fewer files on a real monorepo). Combined effect on a 24k-commit production repo: 80+ minutes to under 3 minutes.
  • validate follows GitHub's actual CODEOWNERS rules: relative patterns (docs/, apps/*, frontend/package.json) are valid, owner-less rules (GitHub's documented exemption mechanism) are valid, escaped spaces are parsed, and ! negation / [...] character ranges are correctly rejected. It previously demanded every pattern start with / or *, failing perfectly valid real-world files. Handle validation now matches GitHub's login rules (no dots, max 39 chars).
  • validate --json exits non-zero on an invalid file, matching the human-readable mode.
  • sync is a no-op success when the generated file matches the committed one ("already in sync"); it previously failed with an empty error because git prints "nothing to commit" on stdout.
  • Downstream commands print a stderr hint when reusing cached state.
  • notifications.include_unchanged now means "also notify when no drift was detected"; without it, no-drift runs no longer fire webhooks.
  • Severity's critical signal honors bus_factor.critical_threshold instead of a hardcoded 1.
  • Review-coverage and balance GitHub scans are bounded to the 200 most recently updated closed PRs and scoped to GITHUB_REPOSITORY; previously unbounded scans exhausted the API rate limit on mature repos.
  • trends counts distinct commits per period; a commit touching 12 files previously counted 12 times.
  • bus-factor, expertise, and onboard share one glob semantic (previously the same pattern matched different path sets per command).
  • Backup-reviewer suggestions fall back to repo-wide top owners for root-level files.
  • Onboarding steps never label a bus_factor<=1 path "easy".
  • Default exclusions now also cover package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, *.min.js, *.min.css, *.map, and the CODEOWNERS file itself (a sync commit would otherwise make whoever runs the tool its inferred owner, perturbing every subsequent run).
  • Composite Action: fails fast with a clear error on shallow clones (fetch-depth: 0 guidance), installs the github extra so handle resolution works in CI, and the PR comment is updated in place (one managed comment per PR, marked resolved when drift clears) instead of posting a new comment on every push.
  • PyGithub moved from a hard dependency to the github extra (with an all convenience extra); core inference is pure git. Unused GitPython dependency dropped.
  • graph DOT export escapes quotes and backslashes in node IDs and labels.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text:
• drift.compare_to config option: it was parsed and documented but never read by any logic. Configs still containing it are ignored, not rejected.
  • Dead internal API surface orphaned by the identity-merge rework: OwnershipMap.handles_only() and github.map_owners().

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Generated CODEOWNERS never emits [...] character ranges: bracket-bearing path segments (Next.js dynamic routes like [companyId]) become the valid * wildcard, colliding patterns merge their owners, and literal spaces in patterns are backslash-escaped. GitHub ignores lines with [...], which silently un-owned those paths. Found by dogfooding against a production Next.js monorepo.
  • Terminal output renders paths like [companyId] verbatim: user-derived text (paths, reasons, handles) is markup-escaped so Rich no longer swallows bracket segments as style tags.
  • Webhook notifications no longer crash the CLI on HTTP or network errors; failures log a warning and notify reports sent: false.
  • Rebalance suggestions can no longer propose shifting reviews onto another overloaded reviewer.
  • Topology reports one mismatch line per overlapping declared team instead of only the first.
  • Tests never touch the developer's real ~/.checkowners (isolated state dir fixture).

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• checkowners github-action: runs the full CI flow (analyze -> drift -> bus-factor -> decay) in one command, writes the checkowners_drift, bus_factor_summary, and decay_summary keys to GITHUB_OUTPUT, and exits non-zero on drift by default (--no-fail-on-drift to override).
  • checkowners trends [--periods N] [--period-days D]: reconstructs the ownership snapshot at the end of each of the last N periods from a single git log pass and reports commits, active contributors, tracked paths, average top-owner confidence, and average bus factor over time.
  • Review-activity factor of the confidence score is now populated (it was previously always 0.0). When github.api_enabled, a token resolves, and GITHUB_REPOSITORY is set, closed-PR reviews are aggregated per changed file and folded into the score; the factor stays 0.0 otherwise.
  • Serialized knowledge-graph cache at ~/.checkowners/graph/<repo-hash>.json, keyed by repo and invalidated by the analysis timestamp; the graph command reuses a fresh cache.
  • Composite Action posts a built-in drift + bus-factor PR comment on pull requests (comment_on_pr input, default true).
  • docs/ directory housing detailed reference: USAGE.md, FAQ.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, this CHANGELOG.md, and the project CODEOWNERS (moved from .github/CODEOWNERS).

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• README drops its Mermaid pipeline diagram (PyPI does not render Mermaid) in favor of a prose summary; the diagram now lives in docs/USAGE.md.
  • paths.exclude default now includes *.generated.*.
  • Composite Action honors its config and mode inputs via the CHECKOWNERS_CONFIG and CHECKOWNERS_DRIFT_MODE environment variables, which load_config now reads.
  • BusFactorReport tiers (tier_for / critical_paths) respect the repo's configured bus_factor thresholds instead of hardcoded defaults.
  • README slimmed to intro, install, quick start, command table, and links to the new docs/.
  • Dogfood config sets output.include_confidence: false so the committed CODEOWNERS no longer publishes a per-file confidence/bus-factor map.
  • All Markdown across the repo follows a tightened style: no em dashes, no typographic -- separators, multi-entry bullets only.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• CI smoke job: pip install "dist/checkowners-"*"-py3-none-any.whl[graph]" failed because bash treated [graph] as a glob character class and never expanded the wildcard. The wheel path is now resolved via ls before installation.
  • Removed dead generate._owners_for_path helper.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• notifications.webhook_url accepts a ${ENV_VAR} reference (e.g. ${CHECKOWNERS_WEBHOOK_URL}) so a committed config can point at a secret/internal endpoint without storing it; an unset variable resolves to "".
  • .checkowners/ is git-ignored so a state or graph cache (contributor emails + ownership map) cannot be committed if CHECKOWNERS_STATE_DIR points inside a repo.
  • github.token remains refused inside .github/checkowners.yml; the only supported way to provide a token is the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Confidence scoring on every path-owner pair. Score is a weighted blend of four signals: commit recency (exponential decay), commit frequency, blame coverage, and PR review activity (last one only when github.api_enabled).
  • Bus factor calculation per path with backup-reviewer suggestions, plus checkowners bus-factor [<path>] [--all].
  • Expertise decay detection that distinguishes dormant from departed owners, recommends transfer targets, and exposes them through checkowners decay.
  • Knowledge graph builder backed by an optional networkx extra: pip install "checkowners[graph]". Render in the terminal or export to DOT via checkowners graph [--export dot].
  • Per-path expertise ranking via checkowners expertise <path>.
  • Team topology inference from commit co-occurrence, with reconciliation against declared GitHub teams when api_enabled. Exposed as checkowners topology.
  • PR review load balancer that detects overloaded reviewers and suggests redistribution. Exposed as checkowners balance.
  • Onboarding path generator that walks the knowledge graph from broad-ownership files to deep-expertise files and emits a Markdown checklist via checkowners onboard <path>.
  • Persistent state cache at ~/.checkowners/state.json (schema v2), with CHECKOWNERS_STATE_DIR override for CI and tests.
  • Composite GitHub Action (action.yml) exposing checkowners_drift, bus_factor_summary, and decay_summary outputs; example workflow at .github/workflows/checkowners-example.yml.
  • Drift severity tiers (low / medium / high / critical) computed from the max confidence delta plus bus-factor and decay signals; notifications.severity_threshold gates webhook delivery.
  • Config sections scoring, decay, bus_factor and new fields on existing sections (confidence_threshold, min_confidence_delta, include_confidence, severity_threshold, github.api_enabled).

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• analysis.lookback_days default lifted from 180 to 365.
  • analysis.top_n_owners default lifted from 2 to 3.
  • paths.exclude default now includes node_modules/**.
  • OwnershipMap reshaped to carry PathOwnership entries (confidence-scored owners, bus factor, decay warnings).
  • DriftResult now carries DriftEntry tuples with per-entry confidence delta and reason.
  • notify payload includes severity, max delta, and per-entry bus factor / decay flags.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: validate strips inline confidence comments so output.include_confidence: true does not fail the validator. Caught while dogfooding.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: github.token is now refused inside .github/checkowners.yml. load_config raises a clear error if the field is present, since that file gets pushed to GitHub. The only supported way to provide a token is the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• GitHub @handle mapping: commit emails are looked up against the GitHub user-search API and rewritten to @username when a match is found.
  • Team and subteam resolution: owner sets whose handles are a subset of an org team collapse to @org/team-slug, with the most deeply-nested matching team winning.
  • CODEOWNERS path auto-detection across .github/CODEOWNERS, root CODEOWNERS, and docs/CODEOWNERS in priority order.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: Deleted files are no longer carried into the generated CODEOWNERS; analyze filters out paths that no longer exist on disk.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: Repo now dogfoods its own generated CODEOWNERS.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Initial CLI: analyze, generate, print, validate, drift, notify, sync.
  • Drift detection with three modes (commit, repo, both) and GITHUB_OUTPUT integration.
  • Webhook notifications on drift events.
  • Syntax-only CODEOWNERS validator.
  • Packaging via hatch; published to PyPI under checkowners.

docs.title: Contributing to CheckOwners
docs.text: Thanks for thinking about contributing. CheckOwners is a pure-git ownership inference engine; this guide covers the local workflow, the conventions enforced by CI, and the PR process.

docs.title: Picking work
docs.text:
Start from a good first issue or any open issue. Every planned change is an issue with a label for the release it ships in, such as v0.7.0, and its "Blocked by" list names what has to merge first. One Upgrade to v0.x.0 issue per release pins and publishes that version.

Usage questions go to Discussions. The issue tracker is for bugs, false positives, and features; those forms are required.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/smusali/checkowners.git
cd checkowners
pip install hatch
hatch run test

hatch run test builds the env (including [graph] and [github] via the dev extra), runs the suite with coverage, fails if total coverage is below 85%, and prints a branch-coverage report for patterns.py, analyze.py, drift.py, and generate.py. Everything else (lint, format, build) flows through the same environment.

Without hatch:

python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e ".[dev]"
pytest

docs.title: Common commands
docs.text:
Command What it does hatch run test pytest with coverage; CI fails below 85% hatch run test -- tests/test_analyze.py --no-cov run a single test file without the coverage floor hatch run test -- -k "test_name" --no-cov run tests matching a substring without the coverage floor hatch run lint ruff check (including S and PTH) + mypy --strict hatch run fmt ruff format hatch build produce sdist and wheel in dist/

The documentation site uses the locked docs requirements. From a clean checkout:

python -m pip install --require-hashes -r requirements-docs.lock
python -m pip install --no-build-isolation --no-deps .
mkdocs build --strict
python tools/check_docs.py site

CI installs from requirements-dev.lock with hashes. A pull request runs pytest on Ubuntu for Python 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14, plus macOS and Windows on Python 3.14, each with the runner's Git. Each of those test jobs stops at 25 minutes. Pushes to main, the nightly schedule, and a manual run repeat the suite on Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows for every supported Python, and also run Ubuntu on Python 3.14 with Git 2.23.0 and Git 2.39.3. The runner's Git is the latest cell. CI then builds the wheel, smoke-tests CLI subcommands against the built artifact (including checkowners[all] and py.typed), and runs ruff plus mypy --strict. Match the pull-request set locally before opening a PR. A green pytest on macOS or Windows runs the same path corpus CI uses: spaces, Unicode, letter case, a long path, and repo-relative separators. The matcher tests also lock forward slashes, backslashes, mixed separators, drive letters, and UNC paths, with no live filesystem.

Optionally, install the pre-commit hooks so ruff, formatting, and mypy run on every commit. This repository also runs checkowners validate when a CODEOWNERS file changes, and checkowners drift on push against .checkowners-baseline.json.

pip install pre-commit
pre-commit install

pre-commit install registers both the commit hook and the push hook (default_install_hook_types). Re-run it after pulling this change if the hooks were already installed. The mypy and checkowners hooks use .venv or venv when one of those directories is present.

docs.title: Branch and PR workflow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    Fork[Fork repo] --> Branch[Topic branch]
    Branch --> Local[Local commits]
    Local --> Push[Push to fork]
    Push --> PR[Open PR to main]
    PR --> CI[CI runs]
    CI --> Review[Maintainer review]
    Review --> Merge[Squash + merge]
  1. Fork the repo and create a branch named after the change (feat/topology-overlap, fix/validate-inline-comments).
  2. Keep commits focused; one conventional commit per logical step. Squash-and-merge is the default, so commit history inside the branch can be granular without polluting main.
  3. Open the PR against main. The PR description should state the user-visible behavior change, link to any related issue, and call out follow-up work that is intentionally out of scope.
  4. Wait for CI; fix anything red. Maintainers review once CI is green.

docs.title: Conventional commits
docs.text:
Every commit on main follows the Conventional Commits spec so the changelog can be generated mechanically:

  • feat(<scope>): <subject> for user-visible additions
  • fix(<scope>): <subject> for bug fixes
  • docs(<scope>): <subject> for documentation
  • chore(<scope>): <subject> for tooling / metadata
  • ci(<scope>): <subject> for workflow changes
  • test(<scope>): <subject> for test-only changes

Scopes match module names (analyze, drift, cli, etc.) or umbrella areas (docs, ci, security). The commit body explains the why and the body lines stay wrapped at 80 columns or so.

docs.title: Code conventions
docs.text:
• Python 3.11 minimum through 3.14. Git 2.23.0 or newer is required at runtime because blame ignore-revs landed in that release. An older Git exits 4 with the version it found and tells you to install a newer Git. Use modern syntax (X | Y unions, dict[str, int]).
  • Python 3.10 is not supported. It reaches upstream end of life in October 2026, and chasing it would only complicate the runtime. The Action installs its own interpreter. Older system Pythons are better served by standalone artifacts than by widening requires-python.
  • Functional style. The only classes allowed are dataclasses in models.py and small frozen dataclasses living inside the module that returns them.
  • Type hints on every function signature; mypy --strict is enforced.
  • All paths via pathlib.Path; never hardcode strings. Ruff PTH enforces this.
  • New CLI subcommand? Wire it in cli.py, give it a --json mode, and persist results through state.write_state when appropriate.
  • Ownership is never binary: every owner carries an ownership_score in [0.0, 1.0] plus a separate evidence_quality.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• Every module has a tests/test_<module>.py.
  • Unit tests mock subprocess calls such as git log and git blame. They do not need a git binary.
  • Integration tests build a temporary repository with the git_repo fixture in tests/conftest.py. Commits pin GIT_AUTHOR_DATE and GIT_COMMITTER_DATE. Mark them @pytest.mark.integration.
  • Drift, patterns, generate, and validate keep both layers: mocked unit tests, and integration tests against a real git history and real CODEOWNERS text.
  • pytest -m integration selects the integration tests. pytest -m "not integration" skips them. The default pytest run includes them, including on every pull request.
  • The integration marker must finish within 60 seconds.
  • tests/test_golden.py is the ownership judgment suite. Histories pin author and committer dates, and analysis uses a fixed as-of. Expected conclusions are keyed by OWNERSHIP_MODEL_VERSION. A model-version change updates that record in the same commit. The beliefs are written in docs/METHODOLOGY.md.
  • Blame-fidelity tests may keep calling init_git_repo and git_commit.
  • Git 2.23.0 or newer is required. The fixture fails if git version is older. The scripted repository used by the integration tests includes spaces, Unicode, a case-distinct path, and a long path. A green run on macOS or Windows executes that same corpus.
  • Tests that touch ~/.checkowners/state.json set the CHECKOWNERS_STATE_DIR env var so they don't clobber the contributor's real state.
  • Coverage is enforced at 85% repo-wide (--cov-fail-under=85); new modules should land above that. The floor is a gate, not a substitute for tests against real git repositories and real CODEOWNERS files. For a focused run that should not apply the floor, pass --no-cov.
  • checkowners/patterns.py also fails CI below 100% branch coverage. The cases live in corpus/compatibility.jsonl (pattern, path, and whole-file rules) and corpus/realworld.jsonl (parser fixtures from permissively licensed public repositories). corpus/README.md is the format other tools can load.
  • Property and differential tests use Hypothesis. HYPOTHESIS_PROFILE=ci (the default) runs 200 examples. HYPOTHESIS_PROFILE=nightly runs 10,000.
  • The nightly Fuzz workflow runs that profile. A shrunk failure is a JSON object with kind, category, pattern, path, and expected. Append it to corpus/compatibility.jsonl and fix the matcher. Do not commit a bot-generated file.

docs.title: Quality bar
docs.text:
The Fuzz workflow's mutation job runs on the nightly cron 0 6 * * * and on workflow_dispatch. It is a sibling of the fuzz job, and it is not in ci.yml. The job sets HYPOTHESIS_PROFILE=ci. One Ubuntu runner and Python 3.14 run five mutmut run calls into one mutants/ directory.

The scopes are:

  • patterns.py, drift.py, and generate.py: every function. Local command: mutmut run "checkowners.patterns.x*", and the same shape for drift and generate.
  • analyze.py scoring: combine_available_signals, signal_weights, signal_reliabilities, frequency_prior_for, _qualify_authors, score_owners, effective_half_life, _as_days, _bounded_half_life, _historical_expertise, _classify_freshness, _recency_score, _elapsed_days, frequency_credit, _frequency_score, and _clamp.
  • github.py identity: resolve_noreply_handle, resolve_handles, _cached_handle, _rate_remaining, _search_budget_allows, _lookup_handle, and _lookup_commit_login.

A scoped local run passes those names as globs, for example mutmut run "checkowners.analyze.x_score_owners*" "checkowners.analyze.x__clamp*".

The score is 100 * killed / (killed + survived). Killed exit codes are 1, 3, and 37. Timeouts stay out of the score. The job fails when a scope has no scored mutants, and when patterns.py is under 90. The other four scopes publish the measured score and have no floor.

This baseline was measured with HYPOTHESIS_PROFILE=ci. pattern_matches returning regex.match(path) is not None is killed.

Scope Killed Survived Score patterns.py 331 9 97.4 drift.py 770 13 98.3 generate.py 622 29 95.5 analyze.py scoring 313 6 98.1 github.py identity 109 1 99.1

These survivors leave behavior unchanged:

  • marker_layout assigns open_line and open_offset when a block opens, so the initial 0 can be None or 1 without being read. The initial manual_done of False can be None: None is falsy, and a completed block assigns True before a repeat is checked.
  • _degenerate_globstar can treat a body of "" as degenerate. The only such pattern is /, and _translate already turns it into a regex that matches nothing.
  • _translate can wrap the empty-pattern regex (?!) in extra literal text. The regex still matches nothing.
  • _translate_segment reads escaped as a flag. None is falsy both at the start and after an escape is consumed.
  • _load_rules, _read_existing, ensure_overwrite_safe, _write_codeowners, and write_github_output can pass encoding=None or encoding="UTF-8" where the source passes "utf-8". "UTF-8" is the same codec. None selects the process locale, and this baseline and the nightly runner use UTF-8, so the CODEOWNERS text is unchanged. Omitting the argument selects that same locale default.
  • _compare assigns changed, notes, and reviews for commit, repo, and both before it builds the result, so an initial None is unused.
  • _find_changed can start team_rules_skipped at None. None is falsy, so a comparison with no team rule still omits the team note.
  • _confidence_delta can return 1.0 for equal casefolded owner sets. _measure_divergence returns before that call when the sets already match.
  • drift_entry_payload and _reconciliation_entry build a one-entry result so compute_severity can score it. That score uses qualified-owner counts, decay, and the confidence delta. drift_detected can be None or False on that temporary result.
  • _as_days can subtract 0.0 instead of adding it. The day count is unchanged.
  • _bounded_half_life can use <= and >= at the floor and ceiling. A cadence equal to either bound still returns that bound.
  • _elapsed_days can treat seconds < 0 like seconds <= 0, treat seconds <= 1 like seconds <= 0, and use / instead of //. Zero and a fraction of a second still return 0, and a positive duration still truncates to whole days.
  • _search_budget_allows can return true after the request budget is already spent. resolve_handles checks that budget again before a search, so no lookup runs and the budget gap is unchanged.
  • generate_codeowners, _build_codeowners_content, and _render_codeowners can default token or org to "XXXX". Team resolution runs only when both values are non-empty, and each mutant changes one default while the other stays "".
  • _read_existing can return "XXXX" for a missing file. That text has no markers, so the manual slice stays empty.
  • _collect_rows can sort with key=None. The path is the first element of each row and paths are unique, so the order matches a path sort.
  • _consolidate can split a root path with split("/") or split("/", 2) instead of split("/", 1). The first segment is the same.
  • _merge_owners can omit score_breakdown=None. None is the field default.
  • _records_for_group looks up paths that are already in the owner map, so the () default can be None or omitted.
  • _resolve_sanitized_rows recurses with per-file rows only. Those rows cannot explode, so file_owners, allow_broad, and depth on the recursive call are unread. On the first call, depth < 1, depth <= 1, and depth < 2 are all true, and exploding a per-file row with or reproduces that row.

A rewritten module gets this baseline recorded again. The workflow summary and the open issue titled Mutation scores show the latest run. This table is the snapshot for the tree that produced it, and the two can diverge until the baseline is recorded again.

The weekly CODEOWNERS conformance workflow (.github/workflows/codeowners-conformance.yml) reruns python tools/build_codeowners_corpus.py conformance --check. It opens or updates an issue titled CODEOWNERS conformance pass rate when the recorded rate drops. It does not commit from CI. Refresh corpus/codeowners_errors.jsonl and corpus/conformance.json locally when the recorded cases change.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text: Runtime dependencies are capped at the next untested major (typer>=0.9.0,<1, rich>=13.0.0,<16, and so on). Bump a ceiling when CI proves the new major. CI installs third-party test and lint deps from requirements-dev.lock with hashes across Python 3.11–3.14, so interpreter-specific pins (today pyyaml-ft) must keep environment markers. The composite Action installs runtime extras from requirements.lock with hashes.

docs.title: Coverage uploads
docs.text: CI uploads coverage.xml to Codecov with the CODECOV_TOKEN repository secret. Install the Codecov GitHub App on the account for PR comments and status checks. If the README badge still 500s after a green upload on main (typical leftover state after an organization move), erase the project in Codecov's Danger Zone and let the next CI run recreate it.

docs.title: Reporting bugs
docs.text:
Open an issue from the issue chooser. Use the bug form for a defect, the false-positive form when inference named the wrong owner, and the feature form for a proposed change. Each form asks for the command, configuration (no tokens), repository shape, and merge strategy. False-positive reports that opt in are added to the public ledger in docs/false-positives.md. A fixed entry keeps the original evidence and names the regression test. An open entry names the tracking issue.

Usage questions belong in Discussions, not the issue tracker.

docs.title: Security issues
docs.text: Do not open public issues for vulnerabilities. Use private vulnerability reporting. You can also email fortyone.technologies@gmail.com with a description and a proof-of-concept. We will respond and coordinate disclosure.

docs.title: Breaking changes
docs.text:
A breaking change is any of:

  • CLI command removal
  • JSON schema changes
  • scoring-model changes
  • default policy changes
  • Action input or output changes
  • configuration schema changes

0.x may include those changes in a minor release when the changelog calls them out. 1.x keeps those contracts stable until a major release.

Scoring, risk classification, and topology each have a model id (model.ownership, model.risk, model.topology). Changing the algorithm bumps that id. Configuration files may pin the ids this release implements; an unknown pin is refused. Cached analyze state and the graph cache are reused only when those ids match.

Append user-visible notes under [Unreleased] in docs/CHANGELOG.md as they merge. Leave [Unreleased] non-empty. A pointer to the next Upgrade to v0.x.0 issue is enough when nothing has landed yet.

docs.title: Semantic versioning
docs.text:
1.0 means the JSON schema, the configuration schema, the CLI, and the exit codes are stable, under the breaking-change definition above. It also means multiple external production users, real issue and pull-request activity, and several outside contributors. No star threshold is required. Usage matters more. Do not rush 1.0.

Until then, 0.x may change those contracts in a minor release when the changelog calls the change out.

docs.title: Governance
docs.text: Project rules live in this guide. The code of conduct covers behavior. Architectural decisions are in Decisions.

docs.title: Maintainers
docs.text:
Samir Musali (@smusali) is the only Core Maintainer, and the only person with release rights. The second maintainer seat is open. It is not filled.

Release rights mean permission to publish a GitHub Release. Publishing a release is what starts the publish workflow.

A person can take the open seat when they already meet the Maintainer rung and a Core Maintainer grants release rights in public.

docs.title: Contributor ladder
docs.text: Rung Criteria Contributor A merged change. Reviewer Repeated review on areas they know. Maintainer Can merge in those areas. Core Maintainer Release rights, and changes to these rules.

docs.title: Open core
docs.text:
The open-source tool is the repository. A commercial layer, if one is ever built, starts at organization-wide features. This document draws the boundary. It does not build the commercial layer.

Open source, forever, no asterisk Commercial layer Single-repository analysis, all commands Cross-repository and organization-wide aggregation Full JSON output, full schema, no gating Historical time-series storage and trend alerting CODEOWNERS generation, drift, validation Organization-level identity graph and team reconciliation Per-repository risk, decay, topology Ranked organization-wide risk register and remediation workflow The Action, the CLI, the pre-commit hook Hosted dashboards, SSO, RBAC, ticket and chat routing The inference spec and conformance corpus Benchmarks against peer organizations

Rules that protect both sides:

  • Do not cripple the open-source tool to sell a paid one.
  • Zero telemetry, ever, by default. CheckOwners does not phone home. Network use is opt-in GitHub API access.
  • A commercial product consumes the open-source JSON contract unmodified. Schema changes ship to open source first.
  • The license stays MIT.
  • The privacy controls are required for this boundary.
  • The validation study is the moat.

docs.title: AI-assisted changes
docs.text: Changes in this repository may be written with agent assistance. Every AI-assisted change is human-reviewed, tested, and signed off before it merges. The README states the same rule in short form. This section is the process.

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text:
One tagged GitHub Release produces the artifacts. Nothing publishes from main by itself.

  1. Set __version__ in checkowners/__init__.py.
  2. Move [Unreleased] to a dated heading ## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD, using the UTC day the version is published to PyPI.
  3. Set version in CITATION.cff to that same version in the same commit.
  4. Keep the Action pin, the committed wheel, and the lockfiles on that version. tools/check_changelog.py rejects a tag whose pins or changelog heading disagree.
  5. Publish the GitHub Release. The tag is vX.Y.Z. The publish workflow checks the changelog, runs hatch build, publishes to PyPI with a GitHub OIDC token, writes a CycloneDX SBOM from requirements.lock, attests the distributions, and uploads the SBOM and provenance to the release.
  6. The docs workflow deploys that version and points the latest alias at it.

There is no Docker image, Homebrew formula, or standalone binary in this repository today. An extra channel, when it exists, publishes from that same tagged release and not from main.

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text: Planned work is an issue labeled for the release it ships in. One upgrade issue per release pins that version. There is no separate roadmap file.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: Supported versions and how to report a vulnerability are in the security policy.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text: Common questions about configuring and operating checkowners. For the full configuration reference see Configuration.

docs.title: Which systems does checkOwners support?
docs.text: Python 3.11 through 3.14, and Git 2.23.0 or newer, on Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows. A pull request checks Ubuntu on every supported Python and macOS plus Windows on Python 3.14. Each of those test jobs is limited to 25 minutes. Pushes to main, the nightly schedule, and a manual run also test Git 2.23.0 and Git 2.39.3 on Ubuntu. The Git already installed on the runner is the latest cell.

docs.title: Why did the command exit 4 and mention Git 2.23.0?
docs.text: Blame needs git blame --ignore-revs-file, which Git added in 2.23.0. The message names the Git it found, or none when git is missing from PATH. Install Git 2.23.0 or newer and rerun. Both cases exit 4.

docs.title: Where is the state directory on Windows?
docs.text: The default is %USERPROFILE%\.checkowners, the same ~/.checkowners directory used on macOS and Linux. CHECKOWNERS_STATE_DIR overrides it and expands a leading ~. Each repository is stored under state/ by a hash of its origin URL, or of its resolved absolute path when it has no origin.

docs.title: Will the generated CODEOWNERS show GitHub usernames or commit email addresses?
docs.text:
GitHub usernames whenever they can be resolved. Start with a .mailmap at the repo root. That is the cheapest accuracy fix and the first identity stage (identity.mailmap: true by default).

Git collapses one person's addresses first. CheckOwners then applies a configured identities entry, parses GitHub noreply emails (12345+login@users.noreply.github.com) to @login locally, reads this repository's handle cache, reads author.login on one local commit, and calls the GitHub user-search API last when GITHUB_TOKEN is set. Search runs only after the commit read found no login. When resolution misses (private email, no GitHub account, API unavailable) the entry falls back to the raw email so the output stays usable.

On squash-merge repos most contributors have noreply author emails, so usernames appear even without a token. An override, a noreply address, or a commit login that shares a handle merges into one owner, and the path's qualified owner count is recomputed over distinct people. A search hit relabels that one email and does not merge two owners. identity.do_not_merge and identity unmerge keep a pair apart. Set identity.mailmap: false to keep raw commit addresses.

contributors.roster can mark someone former. That status is configuration. Org membership and commit dates do not invent it. checkowners simulate --remove-status former removes the cached owners with that status.

identity:
  mailmap: true          # default; set false for raw emails
  negative_cache_ttl_days: 30
github:
  resolve_handles: true  # default
identities:
  "@alice":
    emails: [alice@company.example]
contributors:
  roster:
    "@bob": former

docs.title: Does it handle GitHub teams and subteams?
docs.text:
Yes. When github.org is set and a token is available, checkowners generate collects every team in the org (including nested subteams), and any owner set whose handles are a subset of a team's membership is collapsed to that team. The most deeply-nested matching team wins ties, so subteams are preferred over their parents.

github:
  org: my-org
  resolve_teams: true    # default; emits @my-org/platform/backend etc.

Disable resolve_teams if you want raw @username entries even when a team would match.

Drift asks the opposite question. A token, github.resolve_teams, and github.org expand @org/team to members, including child teams. Without that directory the team rule is unverifiable. It is not reported as aligned. See Drift and severity.

docs.title: Can a report omit people's names?
docs.text:
Yes. output.anonymize: true replaces each person with a stable person- token for that repository. output.aggregate_only: true drops per-person fields and keeps repository metrics. identity.mode is handle (default), email, or hashed. privacy.redact_emails: true or --redact-emails replaces addresses in output with tokens. contributors.exclude removes those people from every command, including graph export.

generate and sync exit 2 under anonymize, aggregate-only, or hashed mode. On disk, state and the per-repository handle files store email tokens rather than raw addresses. See Privacy controls.

docs.title: Does checkowners require a GitHub token?
docs.text:
No. The core inference is pure git and runs offline. A token is only needed for three optional features:

Feature Config gate Why a token is needed Email to @username resolution (non-noreply emails) github.resolve_handles GitHub user-search API Team / subteam resolution github.resolve_teams + github.org List org teams + members Review history and team reconciliation github.api_enabled PR review API + team membership

Noreply emails (login@users.noreply.github.com) resolve to @login without any token. The API-backed features also need the github extra (pip install "checkowners[github]"). Without it they degrade gracefully with a log hint.

Without a token you still get scored ownership, drift detection, qualified owner counts, ownership freshness, and onboarding paths. They operate on email handles and skip the review-activity signal. Remaining weights are renormalized so the score stays on [0, 1]. What that score is, and what it is not, is in Methodology. When it can be wrong is in Limitations.

docs.title: What environment variable holds the token?
docs.text:
GITHUB_TOKEN (not GITHUB_API_KEY). This is the only supported way to provide a token. github.token is intentionally not accepted in checkowners.yml because that file gets committed to git and storing a secret there would publish it to GitHub.

load_config refuses to load a config that contains github.token so a misconfigured repo fails fast instead of silently leaking. The full environment-variable list and precedence live in Environment variables.

export GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_...
checkowners generate

In GitHub Actions the job token exists as ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} / ${{ github.token }}. A run: step only sees GITHUB_TOKEN if the workflow exports it. The composite action does this for you: github_token defaults to ${{ github.token }} and is exported on the github-action step and the PR comment step. Pass a PAT or App token only when the default job token is not enough (org team listing or commenting). See docs/USAGE.md.

- uses: smusali/checkowners@v0
  # github_token defaults to github.token; override only when you need a PAT.
  # @v0 tracks the latest 0.x; @v0.6 tracks 0.6.x; @v0.5 stays on 0.5.x; @v0.6.0 is the pin.
  with:
    github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

If you invoke the CLI yourself in a run: step, export the token:

- run: checkowners drift --json
  env:
    GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

docs.title: What token scopes are needed?
docs.text:
Capability Job token (permissions) Classic PAT Fine-grained PAT Email to @username (user search) Default job token is enough (contents: read is already required for checkout) Authenticated token; read:user if you want the user-search scope stated explicitly No extra repository permission Team / subteam resolution Not available: the default GITHUB_TOKEN is repo-scoped and cannot list org teams. Pass a PAT or App token via github_token read:org Organization members: Read Review coverage and suggest (github.api_enabled) pull-requests: read repo (private) or public_repo Pull requests: Read suggest --pr file list pull-requests: read repo (private) or public_repo Pull requests: Read PR comment (Action comment_on_pr) pull-requests: write repo Pull requests: Write Code scanning upload (upload_sarif) security-events: write Not applicable to a classic PAT for this upload Code scanning alerts: Read and write checkOwners check run checks: write Not applicable to a classic PAT for this check Checks: Read and write Reconciliation pull request (checkowners sync) contents: write and pull-requests: write repo Contents: Read and write, and Pull requests: Read and write

Fork pull_request runs cannot comment or upload code scanning results with the job token: GitHub makes that token read-only regardless of the permissions: block. The action skips the comment, skips the SARIF upload, writes the report and the SARIF artifact, and does not fail the job. The same warning-not-failure path applies when the workflow itself is read-only; set comment_on_pr: false to skip the comment. A check run needs checks: write. Without it the check is skipped and the job result stays the findings exit code.

checkowners sync uses the same token to open a pull request. The repository GITHUB_TOKEN can do that, but GitHub will not run push workflows from it, and the pull_request workflows it creates stay waiting for approval. Use a personal access token or a GitHub App token when those checks should start on their own. --commit commits on the current branch instead. --dry-run only prints the diff.

A fine-grained PAT scoped to the target org with the minimums above is the recommended setup when the job token cannot reach org teams.

docs.title: Can the CODEOWNERS file live in the repo root instead of .github/?
docs.text:
Yes. checkowners auto-detects the file at any of the three locations GitHub itself supports, in priority order:

  1. .github/CODEOWNERS
  2. CODEOWNERS (repo root)
  3. docs/CODEOWNERS

The first one that exists wins for analyze, drift, validate, and sync. If none exists, generate creates .github/CODEOWNERS by default; move the file manually if you want a different layout and checkowners will keep using it there.

Note that generate and sync refuse to overwrite a CODEOWNERS that was not generated by checkOwners (it looks for the machine-generated header). Pass --force to replace a hand-written file, or to write a file larger than output.max_bytes.

docs.title: Where does the config file live?
docs.text: .github/checkowners.yml. There's no auto-detection for the config; it has to live there.

docs.title: Where is the state cache?
docs.text: ~/.checkowners/ (schema 1). checkowners cache path prints that directory. State and graph files are named from the normalized origin URL, so two checkouts of the same remote share a cache. A repo with no origin is keyed by its absolute path, and the stored identity is checked on load, so one repo cannot read another's file. Downstream commands (qualified-owners, decay, topology, suggest, balance, onboard, expertise, graph) reuse the file when its commit is still HEAD and the scoring config hash matches. If not, they apply a usable baseline incrementally, or score the full lookback when the baseline is missing or rejected. A rejected baseline prints the reason on stderr. --no-incremental forces the full lookback. --allow-stale reuses a map from an older commit. --max-age SECONDS refuses a map older than that (0 expires immediately). --no-cache skips the analysis cache and the blame cache for one run. cache clear drops analysis files and blame-cache files and keeps handle files. cache purge deletes the directory contents, including handle tokens and the identity graph. State, graph, and blame-cache files are capped at 256 MiB together and the oldest files are removed past that cap. The blame cache key is the blob SHA, the path, the blame flags, the ignore-revs bytes, the mass-refactor revisions, and the .mailmap bytes. --verbose prints the hit and miss counts. explain and owners do not read this cache. Override the directory with CHECKOWNERS_STATE_DIR for CI or tests. The composite Action uses ~/.checkowners when cache is "true", and ${{ runner.temp }}/checkowners-state when cache is "false". See docs/USAGE.md.

docs.title: How is the ownership score computed?
docs.text:
A weighted mean over available signals, each in [0.0, 1.0]:

  • Recency: exp(-ln 2 × days_since_last_commit / half_life). The default strategy is adaptive: the half-life is the path's median gap between commits, clamped to 14 and 730 days. A path with no gap keeps the 90-day half-life. scoring.recency_strategy: fixed uses that 90-day value for every path.
  • Frequency: contributor's commits on the path divided by the path's max contributor.
  • Blame coverage: fraction of current lines git blame attributes to the contributor, after whitespace ignore, optional move/copy detection, and ignore-revs.
  • Review activity: PR reviews on the path divided by total reviews. Unavailable unless github.api_enabled is true; missing review is skipped, not scored as 0.0.
  • Change survival: current blame lines divided by that person's blame lines at their last commit. Line counts, not an AST diff. Unavailable when blame did not run or the older count is zero. Below 0.2, with a later commit from someone else, the owner is superseded.
ownership_score  = Σ(wᵢ × aᵢ × sᵢ) / Σ(wᵢ × aᵢ)
evidence_quality = Σ(wᵢ × aᵢ × rᵢ) / Σ(wᵢ)

Weights and per-signal *_reliability defaults live under scoring. The score is always on [0.0, 1.0]; owners below analysis.confidence_threshold are dropped from the generated CODEOWNERS. JSON emits ownership_score. This is a ranking signal, not a calibrated probability. The formulas, what each signal proxies, the truck-factor divergence, and the project principles are in Methodology. When the tool can be wrong is in Limitations. If you gate CI on a threshold, re-check it after upgrading: offline scores are no longer capped at 0.85.

docs.title: Can I tune the inference for a high-turnover team?
docs.text:
Yes. Common tunings:

scoring:
  recency_strategy: fixed
  recency_half_life_days: 45   # shorten ownership freshness
  recency_weight: 0.5          # weigh recent commits higher

decay:
  threshold_days: 90           # continuity risk when a path has no commit interval

analysis:
  confidence_threshold: 0.4    # stricter cutoff

docs.title: Why didn't a formatter commit take ownership?
docs.text: Blame ignores whitespace-only edits (-w), follows moved and copied lines when git.detect_moves is true, and omits commits listed in .git-blame-ignore-revs (or blame.ignoreRevsFile). Commits that modify at least git.mass_refactor_file_fraction of tracked files (default half the repository) are omitted the same way, so a black . or license-header sweep does not become the owner. Add the formatting SHA to .git-blame-ignore-revs for an explicit record. Analyze JSON reports whether an ignore-revs file was found, and whether a .mailmap was found and applied, under analysis.

docs.title: Why are some paths missing from checkowners analyze?
docs.text: Four filters can drop a path: .gitattributes marks it linguist-generated or linguist-vendored (analysis.respect_gitattributes, on by default), it matches a paths.exclude pattern (the fallback list), it no longer exists on disk (deleted files are filtered automatically so CODEOWNERS doesn't pin removed paths), or its only contributors are bots (analysis.exclude_bots, on by default). With qualification.strategy: threshold, a fifth filter still drops paths where no contributor reaches analysis.min_commits within the lookback window. The default adaptive strategy keeps those sparse paths and scores them; a one-commit author of a new file can appear as an owner. Analyze JSON reports analysis.excluded_gitattributes and analysis.excluded_static so a path counted under gitattributes is not counted again under the static list.

docs.title: Drift, severity, and CI
docs.text: drift.mode defaults to commit (missing + changed). Set repo or both to also flag stale rules.

docs.title: What does drift "severity" mean in CI?
docs.text:
Severity is the worst entry score. The score mixes overlap, the confidence delta, path criticality, decay, and a bump when one qualified owner remains. The default cutoffs are 0.15 / 0.35 / 0.55 / 0.75, stored as drift.severity_thresholds. Below 0.15 the tier is info. A solo repository is not uniformly critical. policy.drift.fail stays false unless you set it.

checkowners with no subcommand runs checkowners audit. checkowners doctor stops at configuration, plus the bus-factor row. doctor --env reports the environment and does not treat a missing token as a pass. --json and the Action output drift_summary include the severity field so a workflow can branch on it.

docs.title: How do I turn checkOwners on without failing on every existing finding?
docs.text: checkowners baseline create writes .checkowners-baseline.json with today's findings. Pass that file with --baseline, drift.baseline_file, or the Action baseline input. Subsequent runs fail only on findings whose identity is not in the file. Identity is rule plus path plus owner set, so a CODEOWNERS reorder does not invalidate the snapshot. checkowners --exit-zero drift is the other adoption path: findings are still printed, and the process exits 0. See Turning checkOwners on for an existing large repository.

docs.title: What is the difference between a baseline and a suppression?
docs.text: The baseline is a bulk snapshot of current debt so CI can start green. A suppression is a named exception with a mandatory reason and an optional expiry. Use a suppression when you can explain one rule on one path; use the baseline when you need to adopt on a large existing tree. Both counts appear in every drift and Action summary.

docs.title: Why does a suppression require a reason?
docs.text: A reasonless ignore becomes invisible debt. load_config rejects a suppression that omits reason or leaves it blank. Expiry is optional. When expires is set and the analysis date is after that day, the command fails and prints the path, rule, date, and reason. It does not keep suppressing.

docs.title: What happens when I fix a finding that is still in the baseline?
docs.text: The leftover baseline row is reported as stale (stale_baseline). That does not fail the run. Re-run checkowners baseline create to drop rows that no longer exist.

docs.title: How do I fail a PR only on critical drift?
docs.text: The example workflow in .github/workflows/checkowners-example.yml does this with fromJson(steps.checkowners.outputs.drift_summary).severity == 'critical'. The default policy does not fail a pull request for ownership drift or a single expert. Set policy.drift.fail: true, or the Action input fail_on_drift: "true", when that drift should block. fail_on_drift: "false" forces the informational path even when the file says to fail.

docs.title: Why is analysis completeness below 100% on a normal repository?
docs.text:
The run score counts every missing evidence source, not only the four scoring signals.
