docs.title: Concepts
docs.text: Short definitions. Formulas live in Methodology. One-line report terms live in the Glossary.

docs.title: Declared vs observed
docs.text: CODEOWNERS is the declared policy. Git history and, when a provider is configured, reviews are the observed evidence. Drift is the comparison of those two layers. RepositoryAnalyzer.reconcile() also reports declared-local owners from the nearest OWNERS file and nested CODEOWNERS, declared-global owners from the repository CODEOWNERS match, and observed owners at file, directory, package, service, and repository scope.

docs.title: Ownership score
docs.text: ownership_score is a ranking from 0.0 to 1.0 built from the signals that were available for that path. It is not a probability that the person should own the path. The signals and the formula are in Ownership score.

docs.title: Evidence quality
docs.text: evidence_quality is separate from the score. It measures how much of the configured signal weight was observed, scaled by analysis completeness. Two owners can share a score and differ in quality. The definition is in the Glossary.

docs.title: Drift
docs.text: Drift reports where inferred owners and the committed CODEOWNERS rules disagree, with a severity and a maximum score gap. Severity tiers, baselines, and policy are in Drift and severity.

docs.title: Knowledge risk
docs.text: qualified_owner_count is the number of owners at or above the confidence threshold after the displayed list is capped. It is not a truck factor. Truck factor is the separate departure measure from simulate. Concentration, decay, and the repository risk report are in Knowledge concentration.

docs.title: Identity resolution
docs.text: Resolution prefers a configured identity, then .mailmap, a GitHub noreply address, this repository's handle cache, author.login on a local commit, and user search last. Search relabels one email and does not merge two owners. The stages are in Identity resolution.

docs.title: Confidence model
docs.text:
Status: accepted.

Context: a single number was being read as a probability that a person should own a path, and as a measure of how much evidence the run collected.

Decision: ownership_score is a ranking from 0.0 to 1.0 of the signals that were available. evidence_quality stays separate. The score is not a calibrated probability. A measured zero stays a measured zero. A signal that did not run is unavailable, not zero.

Consequences: methodology is the scoring contract. A formula change bumps models.ownership even when the JSON types stay the same. Reports show score and quality side by side.

docs.title: CODEOWNERS pattern engine
docs.text:
Status: accepted.

Context: directory rules and GitHub's last-match-wins behavior were being compared as literal strings, which marked real files missing.

Decision: pattern matching follows GitHub CODEOWNERS semantics in checkowners.patterns. The last matching pattern in file order assigns the owners. GitLab sections are a dialect on that engine, not a second matcher. Bitbucket and Gerrit names are recognized and are not rendered.

Consequences: generate and validate share the engine. A new forge adds a writer. It does not fork the matcher.

docs.title: Identity resolution
docs.text:
Status: accepted.

Context: one person shows up as several emails, and a remote search that merges those emails can collapse two people.

Decision: resolution order is a configured identities entry, .mailmap when identity.mailmap is on, a GitHub noreply address, this repository's handle cache, author.login on one local commit, and user search last. Search relabels that one email. It does not merge two owners. identity.do_not_merge and identity unmerge keep a pair apart. A miss expires after identity.negative_cache_ttl_days.

Consequences: .mailmap is the cheapest accuracy fix. Search stays last and local. contributors.roster sets contributor_status. Commit dates do not invent former.

docs.title: Knowledge concentration
docs.text:
Status: accepted.

Context: the capped count of owners above the confidence threshold was labeled bus factor. That name claims a removal simulation the count does not perform.

Decision: the count is qualified_owner_count, taken from the list already truncated to analysis.top_n_owners. The bus_factor config section classifies that capped count. Truck factor stays the departure measure: on one path, the smallest number of highest-share contributors whose scores reach a configured fraction, and in simulate, the number of authors whose departure drops file coverage below the first threshold.

Consequences: raising top_n_owners raises the maximum reportable count without any code changing hands. Concentration metrics use every score at or above the threshold, before that truncation. The displayed owner list stays truncated.

docs.title: Notifier
docs.text:
Status: accepted.

Context: a built-in webhook posts repository findings to a URL the tool chooses, and a network error in that post becomes a failure of the audit.

Decision: CheckOwners does not send webhooks. The Action writes bounded summaries to its outputs. The caller posts those summaries. A Slack step that reads drift_summary is the caller's workflow, not a client inside the tool.

Consequences: there is no notification setting in the config file. Delivery, routing, and retries belong to the workflow that already has the secret.

docs.title: Blame architecture
docs.text:
Status: accepted.

Context: one git blame process per file spends time on process startup. Three replacements were timed: git blame --incremental, one git log --numstat pass, and in-process blame through pygit2. Production attribution had to stay identical to git blame --line-porcelain.

Decision: production blame stays git blame --line-porcelain, one process per path, on a thread pool. On the recorded run, incremental blame was not faster (0.3498 seconds versus 0.3487 on the ci tier, and 8.8745 versus 8.722 on 2000 files) and numstat was faster (0.0223 and 0.0233 seconds) without matching porcelain attribution. pygit2 stays a benchmark probe. It is not the analyze path. owners, explain, and change blame only the path they were asked about. Unchanged blobs hit the blame cache.

Consequences: pure git remains the runtime dependency. A later replacement has to match porcelain line attribution or document a model change. The recorded choice is porcelain.

docs.title: Forge abstraction
docs.text:
Status: accepted.

Context: ownership evidence is not GitHub-specific, and folding every forge into the scorer would put host-specific conditionals in the scoring path.

Decision: --dialect accepts github, gitlab, bitbucket, and gerrit. GitHub and GitLab render. Bitbucket and Gerrit exit 2 until a writer exists. RepositoryAnalyzer is the library entry. analyze() returns scored ownership with the commit, blame, and review observations stored on each path. Scoring can run again from those stored observations. GitHub remains the best-supported host. New forges wait on demand.

Consequences: a model change can be evaluated against stored evidence without another git or API pass. Adding a forge is a writer and a client behind the dialect seam, not an edit to the score formula.

docs.title: False positives
docs.text:
A false positive is a case where the scored owner and the maintainer's judgment disagree. The prediction and the repository evidence stay in the record. The correction sits beside them.

Submit a correction with the false-positive issue form. Say whether the anonymized report may be added here. A fixed entry names the regression test that locks the correction. An open entry names the issue that tracks it.

docs.title: formatting-reindent
docs.text:
Prediction: Bob is the owner of foo.py because a reformat commit touches the file.

Judgment: Alice remains the primary owner. Bob's blame share is 0.

Reason: A whitespace reformat does not confer ownership.

Fix: Blame share for the reformat is 0, so Bob scores below Alice.

Category: recommendation_wrong. Status: fixed. Test: test_golden_formatting.

Evidence: Alice creates and edits foo.py. Bob reindents it. Alice reviewed that change. The reformat commit and Bob's zero blame share stay in the record.

docs.title: Monorepos
docs.text: output.consolidate collapses a directory into one rule when every inferred file under it shares an owner set. analysis.follow_renames keeps history on the current path after a rename or same-commit copy. A repository that is already large should start with the large-repository rollout instead of failing CI on the first drift run. Sample configs are in the examples directory.

docs.title: GitHub teams
docs.text: Set github.org and leave github.resolve_teams on when a rule should name @org/team instead of the expanded members. Team checks and review coverage need github.api_enabled and GITHUB_TOKEN. An offline run does not treat a cached team answer as aligned. Token scopes are in the FAQ.

docs.title: Existing CODEOWNERS
docs.text: generate keeps a # checkowners:manual block byte for byte and rewrites only the generated block. output.block_order chooses which block wins when they overlap. drift reports a manual rule that differs from observed expertise for review rather than as changed. The file layout is in Generated CODEOWNERS.

docs.title: Large repositories
docs.text:
Enabling drift on a repository that already has thousands of mismatches fails CI on day one. Capture today's findings, commit the file, and fail only on new ones.

checkowners baseline create
git add .checkowners-baseline.json

Then pass the file to every gate:

checkowners drift --baseline .checkowners-baseline.json

Or set drift.baseline_file: .checkowners-baseline.json in .github/checkowners.yml, or pass the Action baseline input (exported as CHECKOWNERS_BASELINE). The CLI flag wins over the environment variable, which wins over the config key. The pre-commit drift hook expects .checkowners-baseline.json at the repository root.

The file is JSON (schema_version: "1") with a sorted findings list. Each finding is identified by rule plus path plus owners. Line numbers and CODEOWNERS order are not part of the identity, so reordering the file does not invalidate the baseline.

Rules that can appear: missing, stale, changed, single-expert (qualified-owner critical paths), and invalid-owner. Decay is not snapshotted.

When a finding is genuinely fixed, the matching baseline row is reported as stale (stale_baseline in JSON and "Stale baseline" in the summary). That does not fail the run. Re-run checkowners baseline create to shrink the file.

docs.title: Policy tuning
docs.text:
Start from the default policy. Drift, a single expert, unowned paths, and incomplete analysis warn and do not fail. Invalid owners fail. --exit-zero, placed before the command name, turns exit code 3 into 0 after the report is printed, which is the informational first CI run.

After the baseline is committed, set fail: true on one check at a time. policy.drift is the usual first gate. A novel row fails only when its check has fail: true, or when it sits under security.paths and breaks that block's stricter rule. A baselined or suppressed row is reported and does not fail the run.

security.paths applies minimum_effective_owners, require_declared_owner, and require_active_expert to the paths you name. Leave the list empty until you want that stricter bar. Do not use the baseline to hide a path you intend that block to enforce.

docs.title: Suppression hygiene
docs.text:
For a named exception that should not live in the bulk snapshot, add an explicit suppression. A reason is required. Expiry is optional. An expired row fails the command instead of keeping the silence:

suppressions:
  - path: legacy/**
    rule: single-expert
    expires: 2026-12-31
    reason: "Scheduled for retirement in Q4"

path uses CODEOWNERS pattern matching. rule must be one of missing, stale, changed, single-expert, or invalid-owner. drift and github-action apply suppressions first, then the baseline. Both commands print baselined, suppressed, and stale_baseline counts so the remaining debt stays visible.

A suppression is a named exception, not a second baseline. Remove it when the reason no longer holds. A suppression without a reason, with an unknown rule, or with a date that is not YYYY-MM-DD is a configuration error at load.

docs.title: Offline mode
docs.text: Place --offline before the command name. The run opens no network connection. Review evidence and team verification are unavailable, and the command says so. github.token is rejected in the config file. The only token source is GITHUB_TOKEN, and an offline run does not use it.

docs.title: Security-sensitive repositories
docs.text:
Put the paths that need a higher bar in security.paths. The block can require two effective owners, a declared owner, and an active expert. Privacy controls, including redaction and what the cache holds, are in Privacy.

Zero telemetry, ever, by default. CheckOwners does not phone home. Network use is opt-in GitHub API access.

docs.title: Internals
docs.text: The scoring contract is Methodology. The decisions behind that contract are in Decisions.

docs.title: Pattern semantics
docs.text: Matching is GitHub CODEOWNERS semantics: the last matching pattern in file order assigns the owners. The implementation is checkowners.patterns. generate and validate accept a dialect. GitHub output is the CODEOWNERS file described in Generated CODEOWNERS. GitLab writes one section per top-level directory. Bitbucket and Gerrit are accepted names and exit 2 because those forges are not rendered.

docs.title: Caching
docs.text: Analysis state is cached per repository under ~/.checkowners (override the root with CHECKOWNERS_STATE_DIR). A later command reuses that file when its commit is HEAD, the scoring config hash matches, and the model ids match. Blame line counts are cached by blob SHA, path, blame flags, ignore-revs, mass-refactor revisions, and .mailmap. State, graph, and blame-cache files share a 256 MiB cap and are evicted oldest-first. cache clear removes analysis files and keeps handle files. cache purge deletes the cache directory. Flags and the on-disk layout are in Pipeline.

docs.title: Benchmark methodology
docs.text: benchmarks/harness.py shells out to checkowners analyze. It does not import the scorers. A result records cold runtime, warm runtime, peak resident memory, git command count, GitHub API request count, cache size, and incremental runtime after one new commit. Two runs on the same commit must match the git command count. Pull-request CI runs the synthetic ci tier and passes --counts-only because a hosted runner does not hold the wall-time band. The procedure, tiers, and recorded figures are in the benchmark readme.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text: CheckOwners infers a ranking from repository evidence. That ranking can be wrong. Observed history is evidence, not authority.

docs.title: Where the tool can be wrong
docs.text:
• Git history is not complete human expertise.
  • Squash merges hide authors who are absent from the commit and its Co-authored-by trailers.
  • Blame can over-credit formatting changes.
  • CODEOWNERS may intentionally differ from repository evidence.
  • GitHub team analysis requires API access.
  • Review history availability affects evidence.
  • Historical trend scores use different data.
  • Identity resolution can be ambiguous.

docs.title: What repository evidence can support
docs.text:
• Contribution frequency inside the lookback window.
  • Recency of the last commit on a path.
  • Current-line attribution, after the blame corrections that actually ran.
  • Review participation, when a review provider returned data.
  • Concentrated activity, as score mass on the truncated owner list.
  • Stale CODEOWNERS rules, when declared owners and inferred owners diverge.
  • Changing patterns across trend periods that share the same two signals.
  • Possible continuity risk, classified as inactive, superseded, or departed. stable is not a warning. A path with no commit interval still uses decay.threshold_days.
  • Possible reviewer affinity, from commits or from recorded reviews.

docs.title: What repository evidence cannot prove
docs.text:
• Formal team ownership. Inferred clusters are a hypothesis, not an org chart.
  • Architectural decision authority.
  • Organizational accountability.
  • Operational ownership.
  • Incident responsibility.
  • Compliance responsibility.
  • Security responsibility.
  • Current employment.
  • Reviewer availability.
  • Business ownership.
  • Managerial accountability.

qualified_owner_count is a capped count, not a truck factor. top_owner_share, effective_owners, truck_factor_50, truck_factor_75, and truck_factor_90 describe score mass after the confidence threshold and before top_n_owners truncation. They are not a repository removal simulation. See Methodology.

docs.title: Inferred clusters are not teams
docs.text: checkowners topology uses weighted Louvain. The result changes with --resolution and with the seed. The published run fixes the seed at 0 and reports modularity plus stability across seeds 0 through 4. A chain of collaborators can still be split or joined for reasons that are not team boundaries. Co-change and temporal overlap are not in the weight. Missing review scores are omitted, not treated as zero. A person can be affiliated with a second cluster. That overlap is a threshold on edge weight, not a survey of the organization. Confirm the hypothesis before acting on it.

docs.title: The ownership graph is not a system model
docs.text: The graph has contributors, files, directories, the repository, teams from CODEOWNERS, and CODEOWNERS rules. It does not have packages, services, commits, pull requests, reviews, incidents, or domains. Python import edges are limited to files already in the ownership map. Articulation points, betweenness, orphan files, and a transfer path describe that graph. They do not identify a service owner or a handover plan.

docs.title: Onboarding suggestions are not a curriculum
docs.text: checkowners onboard can order steps from resolved Python imports. It does not know code complexity, test coverage, or documentation coverage, and it says so. A mentor candidate is a qualified owner who is not former, inactive, or bot, ranked by how often someone else also qualifies on the selected steps. The list is not an assignment and it is not a measure of who has time.

docs.title: Git history is incomplete evidence
docs.text:
Git attribution is not a complete engineering contribution history. Analyze reports merge_strategy and co_author_count so that gap is visible. git.merge_strategy: auto detects the dominant style in the lookback window. An explicit squash, merge, or rebase is reported as given. Detection does not change which commits are read. git log walks every parent. It does not pass -m or --first-parent: -m would count a merge's files twice, and --first-parent would hide the authors on the merged branch.

  • auto. If at least 5% of commits in the window have two or more parents, the strategy is merge. Otherwise, if at least half of the remaining commits have a subject ending in (#<number>), the strategy is squash. Otherwise, including an empty window, it is rebase.
  • squash. One commit stands in for the change. Other authors are recovered only from Co-authored-by trailers when git.count_co_authors is true. Each credited person is scored on every file in that commit, with git.co_author_weight relative to the author's 1. Blame still names only the commit author. Reviewers, and authors left off the trailer, are not recovered. Pull-request participant lists are not read.
  • merge. Commits that were merged keep their own files and authors. The merge commit itself adds no file credit. A trailer on a merged commit still credits that co-author.
  • rebase. Each replayed commit keeps its author. A trailer credits an extra person on that commit. It does not stand in for commits the rebase dropped.

git.count_co_authors: false scores only the commit author and reports co_author_count: 0.

A Co-authored-by line counts only in the form Name <email>. The key is case-insensitive. Any other trailer is ignored and does not fail the run. The same email twice on one commit counts once. A trailer that is the author, or that .mailmap maps to the author, is not a second person. Co-author emails use the same .mailmap mapping, bot filter, and handle resolution as authors. Blame does not split lines across co-authors.

  • Unmapped emails stay distinct. .mailmap (on by default) collapses addresses the repository already listed; anything left unmapped is still two identities until handle resolution merges them.
  • History follows renames when analysis.follow_renames is true (the default), using -M and -C at analysis.rename_similarity (default 50). A copy of an unmodified file is not linked, because finding those copies compares the new file with every unchanged file. analysis.follow_renames: false scores each literal path on its own. -M and -C on blame still only attribute lines moved inside one commit. explain lists the prior names used for scoring when follow is on, and the git log --follow name list when it is off.

docs.title: Blame corrections have limits
docs.text:
• Ignore-revs applies only when .git-blame-ignore-revs (or the configured path, or blame.ignoreRevsFile) exists. Repositories that never listed a formatter commit still get mass-refactor omission when that commit modified at least git.mass_refactor_file_fraction of tracked files.
  • Mass-refactor detection is a file-count heuristic on modifications. A large feature that edits half the tree can be omitted from blame the same way a formatter is. Set the fraction to 0 to disable.
  • Whitespace-only edits are ignored (-w). Token-changing formatters still need ignore-revs or the mass-refactor threshold.
  • Blame can still over-credit a formatting change that is not whitespace-only and is below the mass-refactor fraction.

docs.title: CODEOWNERS is policy, not a measurement
docs.text:
CODEOWNERS may intentionally differ from inferred expertise. A security team, a compliance owner, or an on-call rotation can be the right declared owner when git history points at someone else. Drift reports that difference. It does not decide which side should win.

GitHub skips any CODEOWNERS line that uses [ ] as a character range. Paths such as routes/[id]/page.tsx therefore cannot be represented exactly. Generate rewrites bracket segments to * only when every inferred path the wildcard matches shares the same owners. When owners differ, the default is per-file rules rather than a wildcard that assigns review to people who did not earn those paths. Literal fallback lines with [...] are also skipped by GitHub; --allow-broad-patterns opts into the broader * rule.

docs.title: GitHub data is optional and partial
docs.text:
GitHub team analysis requires API access. Without a token that can list the organization, team membership is unverifiable. Offline mode does not call the network.

Review history availability affects evidence. With no review provider, the review signal is unavailable: it is omitted from ownership_score and it lowers evidence_quality. A missing review history is not a score of zero and it is not evidence that nobody reviewed the path.

suggest labels that gap as load_signal: git_authorship_proxy. The JSON field reviews then holds commit totals. Those totals are not review load, and the command does not recommend a person from them. When the API sample exists, the label is github_completed_reviews. The ownership review factor uses pulls closed inside analysis.review_lookback_days, which follows analysis.lookback_days when omitted. Two repositories with the same in-window reviewers and paths get the same review shares even when one ships faster. reviews_sampled is how many closed pulls were included. reviews_window_days is the span back to the oldest of those pulls. A young repository can show a shorter span with no warning, because the pull list ended. A recently updated pull that closed before the window is not part of the signal, but walking those updates can spend analysis.max_api_requests before the window is filled. That stop is a gap whose reason starts with Review window truncated:, and it lowers analysis_completeness. It is not a silent short window. Suggest still reads the 200 most recently updated closed pull requests, and open pull requests, also capped at 200, are only the current waiting queue. median_response_time_hours is pull open to first submitted review, not the time from the review request. pr_complexity is the median number of changed lines, not a calibrated complexity score. review_concentration is per analyzed path, and only when recorded reviews exist.

docs.title: Historical trend scores use different data
docs.text:
trends reconstructs each period from git log only. The series is historical_activity_confidence (model_version historical-v1, signals recency and frequency). avg_qualified_owner_count uses those same scores. ownership_score is ownership-v2 and can include blame, review, and change survival. Change survival compares blame line counts at the current blob and at that person's last commit. It is not an AST comparison. The two numbers are not the same metric. The command prints that limitation. Naming ownership_score in the same report requires --compare-ownership and --acknowledge-different-metrics, and still does not plot ownership_score values on the historical series.

Historical blame is not reconstructed. It stays unavailable until a published benchmark shows the cost is acceptable.

historical_confidence on a continuity-risk warning is the present ownership_score of an owner whose freshness status is not stable. It is not historical_activity_confidence and it is not a score from an earlier period. active_expertise, historical_expertise, and maintenance_recency are evidence scores, not a measurement of what a person knows. historical_expertise does not measure which lines survived.

docs.title: Identity resolution can be ambiguous
docs.text:
• Private emails and accounts that do not appear in the GitHub search API stay unresolved.
  • User search matches a public profile email and can attach the wrong account. A search hit may relabel one email. It does not collapse two owners.
  • Two people who share an address, or one person who never listed both addresses in .mailmap or identities, can be split or merged incorrectly. identity.do_not_merge and identity unmerge keep a named pair apart.
  • Noreply addresses resolve to a login locally. A commit linked to an account resolves from author.login. Other addresses need a configured identity, a cache hit, search, or they remain raw emails.
  • former is roster-only. A person who is not on the roster and is absent from the org is external when the member list was fetched, not former. Commit dates never assign former.
  • A login ending in [bot], an account type of Bot, a known dependency address, bots.additional, or identities.*.service_account is a bot. The substring bot in a human name is not. A long run of identical subjects caps frequency credit and does not delete the author.

docs.title: Completeness is reported, not implied
docs.text: A run with a missing token, a shallow clone, an exhausted API or runtime budget, unresolved identities, or a skipped team comparison still prints an ownership table. The summary includes analysis completeness and one reason per missing source. That percentage is not a finding, and a missing source is not evidence that a person did not do the work. --fail-on-incomplete and policy.incomplete_analysis.fail are how strict CI turns that report into exit code 3.

docs.title: Published reports
docs.text: An HTML report and a public audit are knowledge-risk descriptions. They are not a performance measurement. Each one repeats that limit, states that inference can be wrong, and tells a maintainer how to ask for the repository to be removed: open an issue on the checkOwners project. A maintainer disagreement is recorded in the false-positive ledger beside the original evidence.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Create .github/checkowners.yml. Every field is optional; defaults shown. version: 1 is required. Any other version, or a file with no version, is refused.

The numbers below are the runtime defaults. Longer-term proposals (max_owners: 5, different signal weights) are not applied here.

version: 1

analysis:
  lookback_days: 365          # integer days, or adaptive (history until the analysis instant)
  review_lookback_days: 365   # positive integer; omit to follow lookback_days, including adaptive
  max_owners: 3               # was analysis.top_n_owners
  confidence_threshold: 0.3   # owners below this are dropped from CODEOWNERS
  respect_gitattributes: true # linguist-generated / linguist-vendored exclude paths first
  max_runtime_seconds: 300    # stop blame when this elapses and mark the run incomplete
  max_git_workers: 16         # parallel git blame processes
  max_api_requests: 2000      # stop GitHub calls at this count and mark the run incomplete
  follow_renames: true        # roll history onto the current path after a rename
  rename_similarity: 50       # percent, 1 to 100; git's default similarity

qualification:
  strategy: adaptive          # adaptive | threshold
  min_commits: 1              # was analysis.min_commits; this key wins if both are set
  strong_blame_override: 0.5  # adaptive: keep authors at or above this blame share

model:
  ownership: ownership-v2     # pin must match this release, or be omitted
  risk: risk-v1
  topology: topology-v2
  signals:
    recency:
      weight: 0.30
      strategy: adaptive      # adaptive | fixed; fixed uses half_life_days for every path
      half_life_days: 90      # fixed half-life, and the fallback when a path has no interval
      half_life_floor_days: 14
      half_life_ceiling_days: 730
      reliability: 1.0
    frequency:
      weight: 0.20
      reliability: 1.0
    blame:
      weight: 0.20
      reliability: 1.0
    reviews:
      weight: 0.15           # skipped (not zeroed) when github.api_enabled is false
      reliability: 1.0
    change_survival:
      weight: 0.15           # skipped when blame did not run; a zero denominator is unavailable
      reliability: 1.0

bots:
  exclude: true               # was analysis.exclude_bots; drop dependabot[bot] and similar
  additional: []              # extra addresses or handles treated as bots

decay:
  threshold_days: 180         # continuity risk when a path has no commit interval
  alert_on_decay: true

bus_factor:
  critical_threshold: 1
  warn_threshold: 2

criticality:
  "payments/**": 1.0         # first matching pattern wins; unmatched paths weigh 1.0
  "auth/**": 1.0
  "analytics/**": 0.6
  "docs/**": 0.1

risk:
  truck_factor_thresholds: [0.50, 0.75, 0.90]

paths:
  exclude:
    - "*.lock"               # fallback when gitattributes do not mark the path
    - "package-lock.json"
    - "pnpm-lock.yaml"
    - "dist/**"
    - "vendor/**"
    - "node_modules/**"
    - "*.generated.*"
    - "*.min.js"
    - "*.min.css"
    - "*.map"
    - "*.whl"
    - ".github/CODEOWNERS"   # the generated file itself is never inferred
    - "CODEOWNERS"
    - "docs/CODEOWNERS"
    - ".checkowners-baseline.json"

output:
  header: "# Generated by checkOwners. Do not edit manually."
  include_unowned: false
  include_confidence: false   # if true, append "# alice(0.92) bob(0.71)" to each line
  consolidate: true           # collapse uniform directories into one dir/ rule
  max_bytes: 2500000          # refuse to write above this without --force (GitHub ignores files over 3 MB)
  verify_round_trip: true     # re-resolve every generated path; fail on mismatch
  allow_broad_patterns: false # emit * wildcards even when they cover extra paths with different owners
  anonymize: false           # stable person tokens; no real names in output
  aggregate_only: false      # drop per-person fields; keep repository metrics
  block_order: manual-first  # manual-first | generated-first; the later block wins overlaps

drift:
  mode: commit                # commit | repo | both
  min_confidence_delta: 0.2   # suppress small-delta drift
  hysteresis_runs: 1          # severity flips on first observation; raise to require N runs
  baseline_file: ""           # accepted-findings file; fail only on new findings
  severity_thresholds: [0.15, 0.35, 0.55, 0.75]  # info, low, medium, high, critical

suppressions: []              # explicit, reason-required; see the adoption guide

github:
  org: ""
  resolve_handles: true       # overrides, noreply, cache, commit login, then search
  resolve_teams: true         # collapse owner sets to a @org/team when possible
  api_enabled: false          # gate review_weight + topology/suggest API features

git:
  blame_ignore_revs_file: .git-blame-ignore-revs
  detect_moves: true          # pass -M and -C to git blame
  mass_refactor_file_fraction: 0.5  # 0 disables; commits that modify this share of tracked files are omitted from blame
  count_co_authors: true      # credit Co-authored-by trailers
  co_author_weight: 1.0       # credit per trailer, relative to the author's 1
  merge_strategy: auto        # auto | squash | merge | rebase

identity:
  mailmap: true               # apply .mailmap in git log and git blame (default; cheapest identity fix)
  mode: handle                # handle | email | hashed
  negative_cache_ttl_days: 30 # how long a failed lookup is remembered; 0 stores no miss
  do_not_merge: []            # pairs that stay two owners even when they share a handle

identities: {}                # "@alice": {emails: [], aliases: [], service_account: false}

privacy:
  redact_emails: false        # replace addresses in output with email tokens

contributors:
  exclude: []                 # omit these people from every command and output
  roster: {}                  # "@bob": former | active | inactive | unknown | bot | external

policy:
  drift:
    fail: false               # stale and changed; set true to block novel ownership drift
    severity: warning         # error | warning; error blocks when fail is omitted
  single_expert:
    fail: false               # qualified-owner critical paths
    severity: warning
  incomplete_analysis:
    fail: false               # same exit as --fail-on-incomplete
    severity: warning
  unowned:
    fail: false               # missing CODEOWNERS coverage
    severity: warning
  invalid_owner:
    fail: true                # syntax and invalid owner tokens
    severity: error

security:
  paths: []                   # empty applies the stricter rules to nothing
  minimum_effective_owners: 2
  require_declared_owner: true
  require_active_expert: true

decay, bus_factor, criticality, risk, paths, output, drift, github, git, identity.mailmap, identity.negative_cache_ttl_days, identity.do_not_merge, identities, contributors.roster, bots.additional, and suppressions are part of this schema. bus_factor is the qualified-owner classifier. criticality is an ordered map of path globs to weights in (0, 1]. risk.truck_factor_thresholds is the three quantiles for truck_factor_50, truck_factor_75, and truck_factor_90. Mailmap is identity.mailmap.

Keys with no implementation yet are refused, including model.signals.historical_depth and git.use_mailmap. policy accepts drift, single_expert, incomplete_analysis, unowned, and invalid_owner, each with fail and severity (error or warning). security accepts paths, minimum_effective_owners, require_declared_owner, and require_active_expert. risk accepts only truck_factor_thresholds. analysis.lookback_days accepts an integer or adaptive. analysis.review_lookback_days accepts a positive integer and, when omitted, uses analysis.lookback_days. git.count_co_authors credits Co-authored-by trailers. git.co_author_weight is that credit relative to the author's 1, in [0, 1]. git.merge_strategy is auto, squash, merge, or rebase. auto reports the dominant style in the lookback window. An explicit value is reported as given. See Limitations.

drift covers stale and changed. unowned covers missing, unowned-file, and observed-unowned. single_expert covers single-expert. invalid_owner covers invalid-owner, owner-permission, invisible-team, empty-team, and file-size. severity: error blocks when fail is omitted. severity: warning does not. When both are set, fail decides the exit and severity is what the report shows. drift and github-action JSON include policy (the resolved checks plus security) and blocking (the novel findings that failed). A path under security.paths blocks when its effective owner count is below minimum_effective_owners, when require_declared_owner is true and the path has no owner, or when require_active_expert is true and every owner with freshness is other than stable. Paths outside that list, including docs/**, keep the global check. The Action fail_on_drift input overrides policy.drift.fail for that run. An empty input uses the file. The reported policy.drift.fail is the value the run used.

Also accepted Same setting analysis.top_n_owners analysis.max_owners analysis.min_commits qualification.min_commits analysis.exclude_bots bots.exclude scoring.recency_weight model.signals.recency.weight scoring.frequency_weight model.signals.frequency.weight scoring.blame_weight model.signals.blame.weight scoring.review_weight model.signals.reviews.weight scoring.recency_half_life_days model.signals.recency.half_life_days scoring.recency_strategy model.signals.recency.strategy scoring.recency_half_life_floor_days model.signals.recency.half_life_floor_days scoring.recency_half_life_ceiling_days model.signals.recency.half_life_ceiling_days scoring.*_reliability model.signals.*.reliability

JSON from every command includes models with ownership, risk, and topology. Human reports print the applicable ids on stderr. Per-repo analyze state and the graph cache are reused only when all three ids match and the scoring config hash matches; a file without models is ignored.

The GitHub token is never read from this file. Set the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable instead. checkowners.yml is committed to your repo, so storing a token here would push it to GitHub. load_config raises a clear error if github.token is present.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Variable Who sets it Role Precedence CHECKOWNERS_CONFIG Action config input, or the user Config file path (relative to repo root, or absolute) Wins over .github/checkowners.yml CHECKOWNERS_DRIFT_MODE Action mode input, or the user commit / repo / both Applied after YAML load; wins over drift.mode CHECKOWNERS_BASELINE Action baseline input, or the user Accepted-findings file path Applied after YAML load; wins over drift.baseline_file CHECKOWNERS_STATE_DIR Action, or the user State / handle / graph cache root Wins over ~/.checkowners GITHUB_TOKEN Action github_token input, or the user Only supported token source Never read from YAML (github.token is rejected) GITHUB_REPOSITORY GitHub runner owner/repo for review coverage, topology, suggest Required for those API features; ignored otherwise GITHUB_OUTPUT GitHub runner github-action writes bounded schema_version: 1 summaries when set Full drift.json / bus_factor.json / decay.json payloads are the uploaded artifact; summaries stay under the 1 MB per-output cap SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH User or CI Integer POSIX seconds used as the analysis instant when --as-of is omitted After --as-of; before HEAD committer time

With cache: "true" (the default), the composite Action sets CHECKOWNERS_STATE_DIR to ~/.checkowners and restores that directory from the Actions cache. cache: "false" skips that restore and sets CHECKOWNERS_STATE_DIR to ${{ runner.temp }}/checkowners-state. CLI and hand-rolled CI must set the variable themselves if they want an ephemeral cache.

docs.title: Calibration
docs.text: calibration is written by checkowners calibrate --fit. It records the cutoff, the train and held-out path counts, the history length, the fitted weights, the default weights, and the held-out precision, recall, MRR, and Brier score. It is not a hand-written defaults block. The command refuses when history spans fewer than 180 days or fewer than 30 labeled paths.

docs.title: JSON schema
docs.text:
The machine-readable contract for --json is commands-v1.json (JSON Schema draft 2020-12). SARIF output is checked against sarif-2.1.0.json.

Every --json command emits schema 1. The document is docs/schemas/commands-v1.json (JSON Schema draft 2020-12). Each command is #/$defs/<command>. who uses owners.

Shared fields on every command:

Field Meaning schema_version "1" checkowners_version The installed package version models ownership, risk, and topology ids repository GITHUB_REPOSITORY when set, otherwise the repo directory name head_sha HEAD at analysis time. Empty when HEAD cannot be read generated_at The analysis instant (--as-of, SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, or HEAD committer time), not the wall clock analysis_completeness Fraction of the evidence catalog that was collected, rounded to 4 decimals. null when the command did not score owners (validate, explain-path, trends). A cached analysis written before this score existed falls back to the signal fraction analysis_gaps Present when the score was computed. Each item is {code, reason} for one missing-evidence source reviews_sampled Closed pull requests included in the ownership review sample. 0 when that sample was not collected reviews_window_days Whole days from the analysis instant back to the oldest included pull. 0 when no pull was included. A young repository can report fewer days than the configured window with no gap

print --json puts path objects under paths, so a file cannot collide with an envelope key. On-disk baselines and ~/.checkowners state are not stamped with this envelope. baseline create --json stdout is.

analyze keeps ignore-revs, mailmap, exclusion counts, merge_strategy, and co_author_count on analysis, next to per-path completeness and signals_available. merge_strategy is squash, merge, or rebase. co_author_count is how many trailers added a person. Per-path completeness is still the fraction of scored (owner, signal) pairs. The envelope analysis_completeness is the run score, not that fraction and not the flag object.

Human summaries print analysis completeness: 73% and one line per gap. An unresolved email comparison stays a note: it does not become a drift finding. A team rule without a directory is unverifiable and keeps the team_membership gap. It is not omitted and it is not aligned. Exhausting max_runtime_seconds, max_api_requests, or the GitHub rate limit records a gap and does not present the truncated run as complete. When review collection is rate limited before any pull is read, the gap reason is Review evidence omitted: GitHub API budget insufficient. When the request budget stops the review window after at least one pull, the reason starts with Review window truncated:.

When a GitHub API call ran in the process, the envelope also includes github_evidence_collected_at and repository_head. team_snapshot is present only when org teams were fetched. Cache-only and noreply-only resolution do not add these fields.

Ownership objects (owners, who, and each path inside analyze and print) use identity, ownership_score, evidence_quality, contributor_status, and flat signals for available signals only. Unavailable signals are omitted. explain names each person with handle and keeps its per-signal breakdown. Risk entries, the risk summary, and the owner distribution include former_knowledge_share. Drift entries include former_owners when that list is not empty. A continuity-risk warning includes contributor_status when the owner is former.

Drift entries add a nested drift object (severity, type, declared_observed_overlap) and recommendation. The flat keys confidence_delta, reason, decay, and qualified_owner_count stay beside those objects.

Stability:

  • The same schema_version may gain an optional property only when this schema file changes in the same commit. Do not remove, rename, or change the type of an existing property.
  • Those breaks bump schema_version.
  • A scoring-formula change bumps models.ownership even when the JSON types stay the same.
  • Action GITHUB_OUTPUT summaries are a separate integer contract, schema_version: 1. Adding fields there is allowed. The drift output is drift_summary. Gates read drift_summary.drift_detected, drift_summary.severity, and bus_factor_summary.critical_paths[0].

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
exit code 0 is success. exit code 1 is an internal error. exit code 2 is a configuration or usage error. exit code 3 is findings. exit code 4 is a git or GitHub integration failure.

Every command uses the same status codes. Any non-zero status fails a shell step and a GitHub Actions step.

Code Meaning 0 Success. No policy violations. 1 Internal error. 2 Configuration or usage error. Bad arguments, invalid config, a missing or unreadable baseline, or a refused overwrite. 3 Findings. validate syntax errors, drift after the baseline ratchet, expired suppressions, and a generate round-trip that does not match. 4 Git or GitHub integration failure. Git could not be run, or Git is older than 2.23.

Place --exit-zero before the command name, same as --as-of:

checkowners --exit-zero drift --json

--exit-zero turns code 3 into 0 after the report is printed. Codes 1, 2, and 4 stay non-zero. Use it for an informational rollout. A baseline file is the other way to adopt without failing on findings that are already accepted.

--fail-on-incomplete, also before the command name, exits 3 when the run completeness score is below 1. policy.incomplete_analysis.fail: true does the same thing. Review evidence, a missing .mailmap, and a missing ignore-revs file are common gaps, so the flag is off by default and a normal run stays 0. --exit-zero still turns that 3 into 0. An analysis with no owners and no stored score has completeness 0, so the flag fails that run. A stored score below 1 fails even when every scored signal happened to be present.

drift and github-action exit 3 when a novel finding's policy check fails. validate exits 3 when a novel invalid-owner finding fails. --fail-on-drift forces policy.drift.fail on for that run, and --no-fail-on-drift forces it off. Omitting the flag uses the configured policy. The default policy does not block drift, single-expert paths, unowned paths, or incomplete analysis. It does block invalid owners. --exit-zero still turns only code 3 into 0. --no-fail-on-drift does not hide config errors, git failures, internal errors, or --fail-on-incomplete.

A git failure is not a clean result. drift no longer treats a failed git ls-files as "no stale rules."
